argument:
Two independent edits inside one contiguous run.

EDIT 1 (@addr tail, engine.s:2407-2416). The low byte of CRTCBASE+w16b is computed into A, parked in Y by `tay` so that the high byte can be computed, then written with `tya / sta SECTAB+1,x`. That detour exists only to keep the carry alive across the store -- but `sta abs,x` sets no flags at all, so C survives it. Storing the low byte straight into SECTAB+1,x and then doing the high byte deletes `tay` (2) and `tya` (2): -4 cycles, -2 bytes, same two bytes end up in the same two slots. A is left holding the high byte rather than the low byte and the final flags come from `adc #>CRTCBASE` rather than `tya`; neither matters -- all three call sites (@emit engine.s:2369, the P2 block engine.s:2323, @setq engine.s:2337) do `lda <something>` as the very next instruction after `jsr @addr`. X is untouched. @addr runs 3-4 times per build_sections, so ~12 cycles/frame.

EDIT 2 (@advance, engine.s:2423-2432) -- this is the bulk. @advance adds ROWCHARS (=80) to the 16-bit w16 exactly Y times, one 8-bit add per row with a carry-propagating `inc w16+1`. That is a multiply by 80 done by repeated addition, and the table of exactly that product already exists and is already used two screens away in this same routine (`sbc mulrowlo,y`, engine.s:2459) and in calc_ring (`lda mulrowlo,x` / `lda mulrowhi,x`, engine.s:2678/2682). Replacing the loop with a single 16-bit table add is a straight re-encoding of the same arithmetic: w16 += 80*Y.

Cost. Old loop body: clc 2, adc# 2, bcc 3 taken (2 + inc w16+1 5 when the low byte wraps), dey 2, bne 3 = 12 cycles per no-carry row, 16 per carry row; plus tay 2, lda w16 3, sta w16 3. The busiest call is the one at @past (engine.s:2321) with tmp4 = VISROWS = 27 rows: 27 additions of 80 produce ~8 carries, so 19*12 + 8*16 - 1 + 8 = ~363 cycles. New code is tay 2, clc 2, lda zp 3, adc abs,y 4, sta zp 3, lda zp 3, adc abs,y 4, sta zp 3 = 24 cycles flat. Saving ~339 on that call. When the run splits (@run takes the `bcc` path and calls @advance twice, engine.s:2309 and 2321) the same 27 rows are split across two calls: old ~370, new 48, saving ~322. Either way it is ~330-340 cycles, plus ~12 from edit 1, so ~351 per build_sections. build_sections runs once per frame from the render path (engine.s:2579, `jsr t_build_sections`), so this is ~351 cycles per frame on every frame. Bytes: @advance grows by 1 (15 -> 16), @addr shrinks by 2, net -1.

Correctness of edit 2. The loop and the table add compute the identical 16-bit sum: mulrowlo/mulrowhi[y] = 80*y (built at engine.s:2770-2781 for x = 0..RINGROWS-1). `clc` is placed before `lda w16` so the first adc is clean; clc does not touch A. Both the old and new versions destroy Y and A and preserve X -- X is live across `jsr @advance` (it is the SECTAB entry index) and neither version touches it. The old version left A = the low byte of w16; the new leaves A = the high byte. Nothing reads it: control falls straight through into @wrap, whose first instruction is `lda w16+1`, and both callers follow the jsr with `lda tmp4` / `lda wfine`. The fall-through into @wrap is preserved. The new form is also strictly safer at Y = 0 (adds 0, where the old `dey / bne` loop would have run 256 times) -- I could not construct a caller that passes 0, but it removes the trap.

I checked every anonymous reference that could count past them. The only references to those two labels are the `bcc :+` at 2428 and the `bne :--` at 2431, both inside the deleted block. Everything before them resolves earlier: @addr's `bcc :++` (2395), `bne :+` (2396) and `bcc :++` (2399) all land on the `:` at 2400 and/or the `:` at 2407, both of which the proposal keeps. There is no `:-` or `:--` anywhere after line 2431 that could reach back across the deleted pair. The `:` at 2407 is retained verbatim in the proposal so the count through @addr is unchanged. Note also that the `:       lda w16b` line that opens `original` is textually identical to engine.s:2400, but the multi-line block is unique (2400 is followed by `sec`, 2407 by `clc`).

argument: Two independent wins on the same straight line, both applying idioms the file already uses twelve lines further down in @air. (a) The asr16 loop. neg16 ends 'sbc var+1 / sta var+1', so A already holds t16+1; asr16 then throws that away and reloads it (lda t16+1, 3) every iteration, and writes it back (ror t16+1, 5). Holding the high byte in A makes each shift cmp #$80 (2) / ror a (2) / ror t16 (5) = 9 instead of 15 -- exactly the 'asr16 x3, high byte held in A' sequence at @air -- and the loop control (ldx #6 / dex / bne, 2 + 5 per iteration) disappears with it because nothing else needs X any more. 6 shifts: 2 + 6*17 + 17(branches) = 121 cycles becomes 54 + 3 (one sta t16+1 to put the high byte back before add16 reads it) = 57. cmp #$80 sets C from the sign bit and ror a rotates it back into bit 7, which is what asr16 does to memory, so the arithmetic is bit-identical. (b) The *24. q6 is a push value in -3..2, so 24*q6 spans -72..+48 and never leaves a signed byte -- the 16-bit sign-extend/shift/copy/add chain (12 + 30 + 12 + 10 + 20 = 84 cycles) can be done in 8 bits: asl x3 gives 8p, asl again 16p, and adc the saved 8p gives 24p, all correct in two's complement for negative q6 ($FE -> $F0 -> $E0, $E0+$F0 = $D0 = -48). sx16 then sign-extends once into t16/t16+1 for add16, 19 + 11 = 30 cycles. (1) The >>6 loop. neg16 ends with 'sta var+1', so A already holds t16+1 -- exactly the fact the @air arm 40 lines below exploits to unroll its three asr16 steps as 'cmp #$80 / ror / ror t16'. Applying the same unroll six times here: the loop costs ldx #6 (2) + 6 iterations of lda t16+1 (3) + cmp #$80 (2) + ror t16+1 (5) + ror t16 (5) + dex (2) + bne (3, 2 on the last) = 2 + 119 = 121 cycles. Held in A it is 6 x (cmp 2 + ror 2 + ror t16 5) = 54, plus sta t16+1 (3) = 57. proposal:
@rowy:  ldy rc_nt
@gl:    lda (ptr),y
        tax
        lda LV_PAGE0,x
        sta GATHERL,y
        lda LV_PAGE0+$100,x
        sta GATHERH,y
        dey
        bpl @gl
        setbank BANK_TILES          ; gather done (it read bank 6); the tiles all live in
                                    ; bank 5, so switch once here, not per tile in @run
        ; ---- draw this char row, and (without re-gathering) the odd row of the same tile row
        jsr @drawrow
        inc rc_y
        dec rc_h
        beq @done
        lda rc_y
        and #1
        beq @nextrow
@second:
        jsr @drawrow
        inc rc_y
        dec rc_h
        beq @done
@nextrow:                           ; one map row on
        lda ptr
        clc
        adc MAPSTRIDE
        sta ptr
        lda ptr+1
        adc MAPSTRIDE+1
        sta ptr+1
        setbank BANK_MAP            ; @drawrow left the tile bank selected
        jmp @rowy
argument: Path changed: the drawrect entry path, taken once per drawrect call. Today the entry falls out of the ptr build and must `bra @rowy` (3 cy) to step over the `setbank BANK_MAP` that only the per-row re-entry needs. Moving that setbank to the tail of @nextrow, where it is the only other producer of control flow into @rowy, makes the entry fall straight into @rowy and removes the bra entirely. Per-row cost is unchanged: before it was `jmp @row` (3) + setbank (lda# 2 + sta ROMSEL_CPY zp 3 + sta ROMSEL abs 4 = 9) = 12 cycles; after it is setbank (9) + `jmp @rowy` (3) = 12. Correctness: at the end of @nextrow A holds ptr+1 and is dead (the next instruction read is `ldy rc_nt`), so setbank's `lda #BANK_MAP` clobbers nothing; no flags are consumed across the jmp; BANK_MAP is still selected before `lda (ptr),y` reads the map. Bytes: the `bra` (2) and one `@row:` label go, the setbank text just moves, net -2. drawrect is called several times a frame (scroll strips, draw_dirty, and via drawrect_clip once per erased sprite), so this is 3 cycles per call, not per tile row - the @gl gather loop itself (30 cy/tile) I could find nothing cheaper for: GATHERL/GATHERH live in the TABLES segment at $0400, not zero page, so the abs,y stores cannot become zp,x, and Y is pinned by `lda (ptr),y` so the gather index cannot move to X.

original:
@nc:    add16i ptr, 640
        ldy #31
:       lda (w16),y
        sta (ptr),y
        dey
        bpl :-
proposal:
@nc:    add16i ptr, 640
        ldy #31
:       lda (w16),y
        sta (ptr),y
        dey
        lda (w16),y
        sta (ptr),y
        dey
        lda (w16),y
        sta (ptr),y
        dey
        lda (w16),y
        sta (ptr),y
        dey
        bpl :-
argument: This is the second of bar_digit's two 32-byte glyph copies, and it is a straight 4x unroll of the copy loop -- no re-ordering, no new registers, no new label. Y runs 31 down to 0: 32 is a multiple of 4, so eight passes of four copies each leave Y at 0 after the 32nd 'sta', and the 32nd 'dey' takes Y to $FF and sets N, so 'bpl :-' falls through exactly as before. Anonymous-label count is unchanged: still exactly one ':' and one ':-' reference to it, so nothing else in logic.s is retargeted. Cost: the loop overhead was 32 x (dey 2 + bpl 3) minus 1 for the final untaken branch = 159 cycles; it becomes 32 x dey (64) + 8 x bpl (24) minus 1 = 87. Saving 72 cycles for 15 extra bytes (three more copies of lda (zp),y / sta (zp),y / dey). The lda/sta page-crossing penalties are identical in both versions so they cancel out of the delta. Path: there is only one path through this window -- bar_digit runs it unconditionally once it gets past the BARCACHE test, i.e. on every digit that actually changed. The identical loop at logic.s:3068-3072 (the first half of the same glyph) would take the same 72 cycles but is outside this window, so I have not touched it.

original:
lda tmp4
        asl
        asl
        asl
        sta ptr                     ; low byte of tmp4*8
        lda tmp4
        lsr
        lsr
        lsr
        lsr
        lsr
        ora #>PARTADDR              ; high byte is tmp4>>5, at most 7
        sta ptr+1
        ; dest pointer adjusted by -wfine so that same Y indexes both
        lda ptr
        sec
        sbc wfine
        sta ptr
        bcs :+
        dec ptr+1
proposal:
lda tmp4
        lsr
        lsr
        lsr
        lsr
        lsr
        ora #>PARTADDR              ; high byte is tmp4>>5, at most 7
        sta ptr+1
        lda tmp4
        asl
        asl
        asl                         ; low byte of tmp4*8
        ; dest pointer adjusted by -wfine so that same Y indexes both
        sec
        sbc wfine
        sta ptr
        bcs :+
        dec ptr+1
argument: Compute the high byte first, then leave the low byte tmp4*8 live in A and subtract wfine from it directly, so the reload 'lda ptr' (3 cycles, 2 bytes) disappears and the only store to ptr is the adjusted one. Instruction by instruction: the five lsr / ora #>PARTADDR / sta ptr+1 group is moved ahead of the three asl group unchanged -- it reads tmp4 and writes only ptr+1, and the asl group reads tmp4 and writes only A, so the two are independent. After the three asl, A is exactly what 'sta ptr' then 'lda ptr' used to reload (sta sets no flags, so the old lda merely re-fetched the same byte). The three asl leave C = bit 5 of tmp4, but 'sec' immediately follows and overwrites it, so sbc is unaffected. sbc wfine / sta ptr / bcs :+ / dec ptr+1 are byte-identical and the anonymous-label count is unchanged (the ':' after 'dec ptr+1' is outside both quoted blocks and is not touched). Neither block uses X or Y, and ptr's final value is identical. Path: this is the straight-line setup of copy_partial, executed once per call (once a frame when the top row is partial), before the per-column loop -- so 3 cycles a frame, not 3 per column. Small, but free and 2 bytes shorter.

assumption: mirror_run's return carry is irrelevant (it is re-cleared on that arm); no other branch targets the bare ':' line.
original:
@rowdone:
        ldy rc_sp+1
        cpy #(>RINGEND - 5)
        bcc :+
        lda rc_sp
        ldx rc_w
        jsr mirror_run

        lda rc_sp                   ; next char row: +640 with ring wrap
        clc
        adc #<ROWBYTES
        sta rc_sp
proposal:
@rowdone:
        ldy rc_sp+1
        cpy #(>RINGEND - 5)
        bcc :+
        lda rc_sp
        ldx rc_w
        jsr mirror_run
        clc                         ; only this arm loses the cpy's cleared C
:
        lda rc_sp                   ; next char row: +640 with ring wrap
        adc #<ROWBYTES
        sta rc_sp
argument: Path changed: the common arm of @rowdone, which runs once per char row that drawrect draws. 'cpy #(>RINGEND - 5)' sets C=1 iff rc_sp+1 >= $76; 'bcc :+' is therefore taken exactly when C=0, and 'lda rc_sp' does not touch C, so the 'clc' before 'adc #<ROWBYTES' is provably redundant on that arm. Moving it onto the mirror_run arm (which is the only way C can be anything else, since mirror_run may return with C set) costs that arm nothing extra and saves 2 cycles on every other row. RINGEND=$7B00 so the mirror_run arm is only entered in the last 5 pages of the ring, i.e. roughly the last two of 28 rows, so the fast arm is taken on the large majority of rows. The anonymous-label count is unchanged: the bare ':' line stays exactly where it is, and 'clc' is inserted before it, so 'bcc :+' still lands on the same instruction (lda rc_sp) it did before. Byte count is unchanged (the clc moves). Note the window's @slow block above is reached at most once per row and was left alone.

assumption: No caller of calc_ring reads the carry on return. Verified: engine.s:2558 follows jsr calc_ring with jsr mirror_seek, and menu.s:190 follows jsr m_calc_ring with jsr clear_ring (m_calc_ring is TOMAIN, and pagelogic is documented at engine.s:3683 to pass the carry through, so the carry really is visible to that caller -- it just is not used). The proposal leaves C=1 at @dd where the original left C=0.
original:
@div:   inx
        sec
        sbc #ROWCHARS
        bcs @div                    ; no borrow: high byte unchanged, value still >= 0
        dey
        bpl @div                    ; borrow absorbed by the high byte
proposal:
sec                         ; the loop's own bcs guarantees C=1 all the way
@div:   inx                         ; round, so the only entries needing a sec are
        sbc #ROWCHARS               ; this one and the one after a borrow
        bcs @div                    ; no borrow: high byte unchanged, value still >= 0
        sec                         ; dey does not touch the carry
        dey
        bpl @div                    ; borrow absorbed by the high byte
argument:
This is the S/80 restoring-division loop, the whole cost of calc_ring, run once a frame (engine.s:2558) with ringS < 2560 (the routine's own header comment), so the quotient q = barq is 0..31 and the loop body executes q+1 times.
The sec inside the loop is redundant on the hot path: the only way back to @div from the bcs is with C=1, because bcs taken *means* C=1. It is needed on just two entries -- the first, where the carry arriving from the preceding bcc :+ / sta ringS+1 is unknown, and the one after dey, where the sbc borrowed. Hoisting it to those two sites costs 2 cycles once at entry and 2 cycles per borrow, and saves 2 cycles on every one of the q+1 iterations. dey does not affect the carry, so placing the second sec before the dey (rather than after the bpl, which would need a bra) is free.
Net = 2*(q+1) - 2 - 2*(H+1) = 2*(q - H), where H = ringS+1 is the number of borrows into the high byte (0..9). For the mid-range case q = 16, H = 5 that is 22 cycles; worst case q = 31, H = 9 it is 44; it is never negative (H <= q since 256 > 80). I have quoted 21 as a representative per-call figure. Costs 1 byte.
Correctness: X, Y, A and the arithmetic are untouched -- every sbc still executes with C=1, exactly as before. The only observable difference is the carry at @dd/rts, which is now 1 instead of 0; see the assumption. @div is reached only from the two branches shown, and no anonymous labels are added or removed.

assumption: @drawrow (engine.s:490-504, four lines past the end of this window) always falls through to `lda rc_y / and #1 / beq :+ / lda #32 / : sta rc_sub`, so on return rc_sub is 0 when the rc_y it was called with was even and 32 when it was odd. rc_sub is written at exactly one place in the file (engine.s:504) and read at exactly one other (engine.s:631, inside the run loop, read-only), so it still holds that value when @drawrow returns.
original:
beq @done
        lda rc_y
        and #1
        beq @nextrow
@second:
proposal:
beq @done
        lda rc_sub
        bne @nextrow
@second:
argument: The test decides whether the tile row just gathered needs its second (odd) char row drawn. It runs after `jsr @drawrow` and after `inc rc_y`, so it is testing bit 0 of the *incremented* rc_y: even -> branch to @nextrow, odd -> fall into @second. @drawrow has already computed bit 0 of the *pre-increment* rc_y and left it in rc_sub as 0 (even) or 32 (odd). Post-increment parity is the complement of pre-increment parity, so 'post-inc odd' == 'rc_sub == 0' and 'post-inc even' == 'rc_sub == 32'. Hence `lda rc_y / and #1 / beq @nextrow` is exactly `lda rc_sub / bne @nextrow`. Cycles: lda zp 3 + and #imm 2 + branch = 5 + branch, becomes lda zp 3 + branch = 3 + branch, so 2 cycles saved on both arms; bytes 2+2+2=6 -> 2+2=4. Flags: only the branch consumes them and both arms then either `jsr @drawrow` (which reloads A) or `lda ptr`, so A and the flags are dead immediately afterwards. Path: this is the per-tile-row arm of drawrect's @row loop -- it executes once for every tile row of every rect drawn, i.e. roughly ceil(rows/2) times per drawrect call and ~14 times for a full 27-row redraw. Both arms benefit equally so the frequency split does not matter.

assumption: The AL=0 reset only ever fires when O_CL,y is zero (that is what the existing bne :+ enforces), so hoisting the O_CL test above it cannot change behaviour.
original:
@nostep:
        lda O_AL,y
        cmp #12
        bne :+
        lda O_CL,y
        bne :+
        lda #0                      ; (no stz abs,y either)
        sta O_AL,y
:       lda O_CL,y
        bne @anim
proposal:
@nostep:
        lda O_CL,y
        bne @anim                   ; collected: the AL == 12 reset is gated on CL == 0
        lda O_AL,y                  ; anyway, so test CL once and first
        cmp #12
        bne :+
        lda #0                      ; (no stz abs,y either)
        sta O_AL,y
:
argument: O_CL,y is loaded twice: once to gate the 'AL == 12 and not collected -> AL = 0' reset, and once immediately after to decide whether to skip the collision tests. Because the reset is itself gated on CL == 0, testing CL first is equivalent: if CL != 0 the reset could not have fired and control goes to @anim either way; if CL == 0 the reset test runs exactly as before and control falls through to lda health. Path costs, per star per frame. Collected star (CL != 0), the path this change targets: was lda O_AL,y 4 + cmp 2 + bne taken 3 + lda O_CL,y 4 + bne @anim taken 3 = 16; now lda O_CL,y 4 + bne taken 3 = 7, saving 9. Live star with AL != 12 (the other common case): was 4+2+3+4+2 = 15, now 4+2+4+2+3 = 15, unchanged -- no regression. Live star with AL == 12 (one step in thirteen): was 27, now 21, saving 6. A collected star is not removed from the object list (it animates AL 12..18 and thereafter falls straight through @anim's cmp #18 / bcs @done), so it pays this every frame for the rest of the level, and the fraction of collected stars rises monotonically. Bytes: 22 -> 17. Flags and registers: the fall-through to lda health previously arrived with Z from lda O_CL,y and now arrives with flags from cmp #12 or from sta O_AL,y, but lda health sets its own N,Z for the beq @tryboom that reads them; A is reloaded at both @anim and lda health; X and Y are untouched. Anonymous labels: exactly one ':' line before and after, and the surviving bne :+ still resolves to it with no intervening label, so no branch is retargeted.

assumption: SECIDX is ordinary bss RAM (engine.s:270, `SECIDX: .res 1`), not a hardware register, so writing it has no side effect.
original:
stz SECIDX
        lda DISPSECT
        sta SECIDX
        jsr scan_keys
        jsr sound_tick
proposal:
lda DISPSECT
        sta SECIDX
        jsr scan_keys
        jsr sound_tick
argument: `stz SECIDX` is a dead store: the very next two instructions are `lda DISPSECT` / `sta SECIDX`, with nothing in between that can read SECIDX. SECIDX is declared at engine.s:270 in the bss block as a plain `.res 1`, so it is RAM, not an I/O location with a write side effect; its only reader is `ldx SECIDX` at engine.s:2914, in the T1 arm of this same ISR, which cannot run here because we are inside the handler with I set. stz sets no flags, so removing it changes nothing for the following `lda DISPSECT`, which sets N/Z from the loaded value exactly as before; A, X and Y are untouched either way. stz abs is 4 cycles / 3 bytes. Path: this is the tail of the vsync arm past @noflip, executed once per vsync, i.e. 50 times a second unconditionally - the busiest line in the window and the one being changed.

assumption: w16/w16+1 hold nothing live after this block: the very next uses are `lda rc_x / sta w16` and `lda rc_x+1 / sta w16+1` eleven and seventeen instructions later (engine.s 421-430), and the only read in between is the `adc w16` this proposal deletes. No label between here and there is a jump target from outside drawrect. rc_w is 1..80 and rc_x <= 1023 (the existing comment's 'map width <= 256 tiles').
original:
lda rc_w
        deca
        clc
        adc rc_x
        sta w16
        lda rc_x+1
        adc #0
        lsr a
        ror w16
        lsr a
        ror w16                     ; w16 = tx1
        sta w16+1
        lda rc_x+1
        lsr
        sta tmp
        lda rc_x
        ror
        lsr tmp
        ror                         ; A = tx0 (map width <= 256 tiles)
        sta rc_tx0
        eor #$FF
        sec
        adc w16
proposal:
lda rc_x+1
        lsr
        sta tmp
        lda rc_x
        ror
        lsr tmp
        ror                         ; A = tx0 (map width <= 256 tiles)
        sta rc_tx0
        lda rc_x                    ; tiles-1 = tx1 - tx0 = ((rc_x & 3) + rc_w - 1) >> 2,
        and #3                      ; so tx1 never needs building: max 3 + 80 - 1 = 82,
        clc                         ; one byte, no 16-bit shift, no w16
        adc rc_w
        deca
        lsr
        lsr
argument:
This is the per-rect invariant block, executed once on every drawrect entry (and so on every drawrect_clip, which ends `jmp drawrect`), i.e. on every scroll strip and every sprite erase rect in the frame. It is straight-line: there is only one path, taken 100% of the time.

What it computes: tx1 = (rc_x + rc_w - 1) >> 2 (into w16:w16+1), tx0 = rc_x >> 2 (into rc_tx0, and left in A), then rc_nt = tx1 - tx0 via `eor #$FF / sec / adc w16`.

Two facts. (1) `sta w16+1` is already a dead store: nothing reads w16+1 before `lda rc_x+1 / sta w16+1` overwrites it in the ringaddr setup; only the low byte is read, by `adc w16`. (2) tx1 - tx0 = floor((rc_x + b)/4) - floor(rc_x/4) with b = rc_w-1, which is identically floor(((rc_x & 3) + b)/4). Since rc_x & 3 <= 3 and rc_w <= 80, the sum is at most 82, so the whole thing is an 8-bit computation: no 16-bit add, no double `lsr a / ror w16`, no w16 at all.

The proposal keeps the tx0 half byte-for-byte (same use of tmp, same `sta rc_tx0`) and replaces the tx1 half with `lda rc_x / and #3 / clc / adc rc_w / deca / lsr / lsr`. It ends with A = rc_nt so the existing `sta rc_nt` on the following line still applies unchanged. `deca` cannot underflow: rc_w >= 1 so (rc_x&3) + rc_w >= 1. Checked against the original on rc_x=7,rc_w=10 (3 both ways), rc_x=4,rc_w=4 (0), rc_x=3,rc_w=2 (1), rc_x=1023,rc_w=1 (0).

Cycles. Original, from `lda rc_w` to `adc w16` inclusive: 3+2+2+3+3+3+2+2+5+2+5+3+3+2+3+3+2+5+2+3+2+2+3 = 65. Proposal: 3+2+3+3+2+5+2+3+3+2+2+3+2+2+2 = 39. Saving 26 cycles on the only path, every drawrect entry. Bytes: 40 -> 23, saving 17.

Flags and registers: X and Y are untouched by both versions. The original leaves C from `adc w16`; the proposal leaves C from the final `lsr`. Neither is read: the next carry consumer is `asl` (which sets its own C) in the rc_ro0 shift, and ringaddr's first add is preceded by its own `asl`. tmp is used identically. A on exit is rc_nt in both.

assumption: No interrupt can be taken between the two writes to SECIDX. This is inside irq_handler with I set on entry and no cli anywhere in it, so a T1 or CA1 IRQ cannot intervene; nothing else in the codebase reads SECIDX except irq_handler itself (engine.s:2914, 2953).
original:
lda #$40
        sta VIA_IFR
        stz SECIDX
        lda DISPSECT
        sta SECIDX
proposal:
lda #$40
        sta VIA_IFR
        lda DISPSECT
        sta SECIDX
argument: 'stz SECIDX' is a dead store: the next two instructions unconditionally overwrite SECIDX with DISPSECT, and SECIDX is a plain bss byte (engine.s:270 '.res 1'), not a hardware register, so the intermediate 0 has no side effect. The only reader of SECIDX is the T1 arm of irq_handler (ldx SECIDX at engine.s:2914), which cannot run while we are inside the vsync arm with I set. The flags left behind also match: previously the last flag-setting instruction before 'jsr scan_keys' was 'lda DISPSECT'; it still is. Path: the vsync arm of irq_handler, taken once per 50Hz field, i.e. every frame. 3 cycles and 3 bytes per field. Small, but free and risk-free.

assumption: @advance is entered with A >= 1 (it is: build_sections calls it with tmp2 and tmp4, both non-zero row counts, and the loop is already a do-while that would run 256 times on 0).
original:
@advance:
        tay
        lda w16
:       clc
        adc #ROWCHARS
        bcc :+
        inc w16+1
:       dey
        bne :--
        sta w16
proposal:
@advance:
        tay
        lda w16
        clc
:       adc #ROWCHARS
        bcc :+
        inc w16+1
        clc
:       dey
        bne :--
        sta w16
argument:
The `clc` at the top of the loop body pays 2 cycles on every iteration, but the loop already knows the carry state on both exits from the add: when `bcc :+` is taken C is 0 and the next `adc` needs no clc at all, and only on the fall-through (carry out of adc #80) is C set. So hoist the clc out of the loop and re-clear it only on the carry arm, after `inc w16+1` (inc on memory does not touch C, so C is still 1 there and the explicit clc is required).

Per-iteration cost. Before: no-carry iteration clc 2 + adc 2 + bcc taken 3 + dey 2 + bne 3 = 12; carry iteration clc 2 + adc 2 + bcc not-taken 2 + inc 5 + dey 2 + bne 3 = 16. After: no-carry 10, carry 16, plus one hoisted clc (2) per call. Net = 2 * (non-carry iterations) - 2 per call.

Which path, how often: this is the only loop in @advance and it runs once per row advanced. build_sections calls @advance once at @past with tmp4 (VISROWS or VISROWS-1 rows) and, when the run splits across the ring end, a second time with tmp2, so roughly VISROWS row-iterations per frame in total. w16 walks by 80 each iteration, so the adc carries when the low byte is >= 176, i.e. on about 80/256 = 31% of iterations; ~69% take the 2-cycle saving. For ~25 iterations a frame that is about 34 cycles less the 2-4 cycles of hoisted clc, so ~30 cycles/frame. I quote the per-iteration figure of 2 as saving_cycles, as the brief asks for the path's per-execution number.

Correctness: identical arithmetic (C is 0 at every `adc` in both versions), Y and the dey/bne loop are untouched, and w16+1 is incremented on exactly the same iterations. Flags on exit: unchanged -- the loop falls out of `bne :--` with Y = 0 and then `sta w16`, which sets no flags, in both versions.

Anonymous labels: the count is unchanged at two. The first `:` moves from the `clc` to the `adc #ROWCHARS` (the instruction that used to follow it) and the second stays on `dey`, so `bcc :+` still targets the `dey` label and `bne :--` still targets the loop-top label. No branch anywhere crosses the moved label.

Bytes: +1 (a second one-byte clc). This is the one place I am paying a byte for cycles, which the brief's ordering (cycles first, bytes second) permits.

assumption: spx/spy (engine.s .zeropage) do not overlap px/py (logic.s .zeropage) -- they are separate .res allocations in the same ZEROPAGE segment, so the early 'sta spx' cannot disturb the later 'sbc px'. This is the same assumption the existing 'sta spx+1' before 'sbc px+1' already makes.
original:
lda O_XL,y                  ; rx/ry = object relative to the player
        sec
        sbc px
        sta rx
        lda O_XH,y
        sta spx+1                   ; sta touches no flags, so C survives for the sbc
        sbc px+1
        sta rx+1
        lda O_YL,y
        sta spy
        sec
        sbc py
        sta ry
        lda O_YH,y
        sbc py+1
        sta ry+1
        lda O_XL,y                  ; spx/spy = where it draws
        sta spx
        lda O_YH,y
        sta spy+1
proposal:
lda O_XL,y                  ; rx/ry = object relative to the player
        sta spx                     ; spx/spy = where it draws: sta touches no flags,
        sec                         ; so the source byte can be banked on the way past
        sbc px
        sta rx
        lda O_XH,y
        sta spx+1                   ; sta touches no flags, so C survives for the sbc
        sbc px+1
        sta rx+1
        lda O_YL,y
        sta spy
        sec
        sbc py
        sta ry
        lda O_YH,y
        sta spy+1
        sbc py+1
        sta ry+1
argument: Path changed: the @lean prologue of process_object, run once for every non-star object in range per logic step -- the only path into the handler table for those objects, so it is the window's busiest line. The routine already banks O_XH,y into spx+1 on the way past (the comment says why it is safe), and banks O_YL,y into spy, but then re-reads O_XL,y and O_YH,y at the end to fill spx and spy+1. Doing the same thing for those two: 'sta spx' after 'lda O_XL,y' and before the 'sec' (sta sets no flags, and sec follows anyway, so the subsequent 'sbc px' is unaffected), and 'sta spy+1' between 'lda O_YH,y' and 'sbc py+1' (sta sets no flags so the borrow from the low-byte 'sbc py' still reaches 'sbc py+1' intact). That makes the trailing four instructions dead and they are deleted. Cost: removed lda O_XL,y 4 + sta spx 3 + lda O_YH,y 4 + sta spy+1 3 = 14 cycles and 3+2+3+2 = 10 bytes; added sta spx 3 + sta spy+1 3 = 6 cycles and 4 bytes. Net 8 cycles and 6 bytes per call (more if O_XL/O_YH cross a page for this Y, since the deleted loads are abs,y). The block contains no labels, so nothing can jump into the middle of it; @call and @tab that follow are untouched, and A/X/Y and the flags at the end are unchanged (the last instruction is still 'sta ry+1' and A still holds ry+1's value, after which 'lda otype' reloads A).

original:

        staz rp                     ; sta (rp) - offset 0 needs no index

        sta spx
        sta (rp),y

        lda SPRLIST+2,x
        sta spx+1
        sta (rp),y

        sta (rp),y

        sta spy+1
        sta (rp),y

        lda #0
        sta (rp),y

proposal:
@write: ldy #1
        lda SPRLIST+1,x
        sta spx
        sta (rp),y
        iny
        lda SPRLIST+2,x
        sta spx+1
        sta (rp),y
        iny
        lda SPRLIST+3,x

        sta (rp),y

        sta (rp),y
        ldy #8
        lda #0
        sta (rp),y

argument: The block loads SPRLIST,x twice: once at the top to write record offset 0, and once at the bottom to pass the id to drawsprite. The two loads are separated only because lda #0/lda SPRLIST+n,x clobber A in between. Moving the pair 'lda SPRLIST,x / staz rp' to the bottom makes the second load serve both purposes: staz rp (sta (rp)) writes offset 0 and leaves A holding the id for the jsr. Nothing in the block reads (rp) offset 0, so the write may be reordered to last; X is untouched throughout (only A and Y move); the store order of offsets 1..4 and 8 is unchanged. Flags: staz rp sets none, so drawsprite is entered with exactly the flags lda SPRLIST,x left, the same as before. Saves one lda abs,x = 4 cycles and 3 bytes. Path: @write, i.e. every sprite that is actually drawn, on both passes of draw_sprites, so ~NSPR times a frame -- the only sprites that skip it are kept box stars that take bpl @next.

assumption: SPRLIST is an absolute table, so lda SPRLIST,x costs 4 cycles (5 only if X crosses a page within the table); no code between the cmp #BOXID0+BOXN and @write alters A on the bcc path.
original:

        cmp #BOXID0+BOXN            ; a box star the logic says nothing can disturb, and
        bcc @write                  ; the same frame already in the same place: if
        ldy spi                     ; nothing has been repainted under it, its pixels
        lda KEEP,y                  ; are still right, so leave it alone
        cmp #2
        bne @write
        ldy #9                      ; and it was not cut off at a window edge, so all
        lda (rp),y                  ; of it is on screen and still intact
        bpl @next
@write: lda SPRLIST,x
proposal:
lda SPRLIST,x
        cmp #BOXID0+BOXN            ; a box star the logic says nothing can disturb, and
        bcc @write                  ; the same frame already in the same place: if
        ldy spi                     ; nothing has been repainted under it, its pixels
        lda KEEP,y                  ; are still right, so leave it alone
        cmp #2
        bne @wrl
        ldy #9                      ; and it was not cut off at a window edge, so all
        lda (rp),y                  ; of it is on screen and still intact
        bpl @next

@write:
argument: There are exactly two branches into @write (engine.s:1039 bcc, :1043 bne) and one fall-through that is impossible (the bpl @next / @write pair means the fall-through from bpl reaches @write too -- that is the third entry). On the bcc path A already holds SPRLIST,x from the load two instructions earlier, so the lda SPRLIST,x at @write is pure reload; on the KEEP path A holds KEEP,y and on the (rp),y fall-through A holds the record byte, so those two do need it. Splitting the label puts the reload only on the two paths that need it. Cost accounting: the bcc path is the dominant one -- in pass 0 every non-box sprite reaches here with id < BOXID0, so cmp #BOXID0+BOXN always sets C=0 and the bcc is taken; in pass 1 every real box (BOXID0 <= id < BOXID0+BOXN) also takes it, and only the 'undisturbable' alias ids fall through to the KEEP test. So essentially every sprite that is actually drawn saves the 4 cycles, at the cost of 3 bytes for the duplicated lda. Flags: staz rp / ldy #1 follow and read no flags, and sta sets none, so the flag state at @write is irrelevant. X and Y are untouched by the change (the new lda SPRLIST,x sits after lda (rp),y, where Y=9 is already dead). No anonymous labels are added or removed -- @wrl is a named cheap-local label.

assumption: Nothing reads qy between the mov16 and the add16i (it does not: the next instruction is 'lda dpx+1').
proposal:
@hl:    mov16 qx, px
        clc
        lda py
        adc #16
        sta qy
        lda py+1
        adc #0
        sta qy+1
argument: This is a surviving mov16+add16i pair: 'qy = py' then 'qy = qy + 16' is just 'qy = py + 16'. mov16 qy,py is lda/sta/lda/sta = 12 cycles, 8 bytes; add16i qy,16 is clc/lda/adc/sta/lda/adc/sta = 18 cycles, 13 bytes; total 30 cycles, 21 bytes. The fused form is clc(2)+lda py(3)+adc #16(2)+sta qy(3)+lda py+1(3)+adc #0(2)+sta qy+1(3) = 18 cycles, 13 bytes. Saving 12 cycles, 8 bytes. Correctness: C is set to 0 by the same clc; the low add is identical; the high add now reads py+1 instead of the just-stored copy of py+1, which holds the same value; the carry between the two adcs is untouched by the intervening sta. Flags at the end are those of 'adc #0' on the same value as before, and the next instruction ('lda dpx+1') overwrites them anyway. qx is untouched. Note this exact fused idiom already appears twice in the same routine (logic.s ~1239 and at @upl ~1305: 'clc / lda py / adc #16 / sta qy / lda py+1 / adc #0 / sta qy+1'), so the rewrite matches existing house style. Path: @hl is the top of the horizontal step loop, executed once per pixel of horizontal movement (|steps| = (vx+128)>>8, typically 1-3) every frame the player is moving; it is the only path through this window.

assumption: @mul is only ever entered by falling through from the 'beq @mdone' above (no other branch targets it) - verified, the only reference is the 'bne @mul' at the loop foot.
original:
lda sp_ptr+1
        sta sp_col+1
        lda sp_ptr
        ldx sp_c
        beq @mdone
@mul:   clc
        adc sp_lines
        bcc :+
        inc sp_col+1
:       dex
        bne @mul
@mdone: sta sp_col
proposal:
lda sp_ptr+1
        sta sp_col+1
        lda sp_ptr
        ldx sp_c
        beq @mdone
        clc
@mul:   adc sp_lines
        bcc :+
        inc sp_col+1
        clc
:       dex
        bne @mul
@mdone: sta sp_col
argument: Path changed: the sp_col = sp_ptr + sp_c*sp_lines repeated-addition loop. It is skipped entirely (beq @mdone) for the ordinary unmirrored, unclipped sprite because @cpos does 'stza sp_c'; it runs sp_c times for mirrored sprites, where the code just above sets sp_c = sp_w-1-sp_c, i.e. about sp_w-1 iterations, and sprite widths here are in 2-pixel chars so sp_w is typically 6-13. Roughly half the sprites on screen face left, so this is a per-mirrored-sprite saving. The loop's 'clc' only has work to do on an iteration whose 'adc' carried; on every other iteration 'bcc :+' has already established C=0 for the next 'adc'. Hoisting the clc to the loop entry and adding one inside the carry arm (after 'inc sp_col+1', which does not affect C) makes the common iteration adc(3)+bcc taken(3)+dex(2)+bne(3) = 11 instead of clc(2)+adc(3)+bcc(3)+dex(2)+bne(3) = 13, and leaves the carrying iteration at 17 cycles exactly as before. Net = 2*(sp_c-1) cycles: 0 at sp_c=1 (never a loss), 10 at sp_c=6, 24 at sp_c=13. The entry clc is needed because C is unknown on the copy-blitter arm ('ldx #8 / bne :++' preserves whatever the mirror subtract left); it is not free to omit even though the other arm's 'asl' of (sp_flags & 3) does leave C=0. One extra byte for the second clc. The anonymous-label count is unchanged - the bare ':' line is still there, in the same place relative to 'bcc :+'.

assumption: BARADDR stays low enough that ptr+1 (<= 3) + >BARADDR cannot carry; it is $7B00 today, so the margin is large. The first clc removal holds unconditionally.
original:
asl
        rol ptr+1
        asl
        rol ptr+1
        clc
        adc #<BARADDR               ; straight into the back buffer's bar row (no offscreen
        sta ptr                     ; buffer): bank 4 glyph at $8xxx, screen bar at $7Bxx
        lda ptr+1
        adc #>BARADDR

        ldy #31
:       lda (w16),y
        sta (ptr),y
        dey
        bpl :-
        lda w16
        clc
        adc #32
        sta w16
proposal:
asl
        rol ptr+1
        asl
        rol ptr+1
        adc #<BARADDR               ; straight into the back buffer's bar row (no offscreen
        sta ptr                     ; buffer): bank 4 glyph at $8xxx, screen bar at $7Bxx
        lda ptr+1                   ; C is already clear: ptr+1 was 0 or 1 before the second
        adc #>BARADDR               ; rol, so that rol shifted a 0 out
        sta ptr+1
        ldy #31
:       lda (w16),y
        sta (ptr),y
        dey
        bpl :-
        lda w16
        adc #32                     ; C still clear: ptr+1 <= 3 and >BARADDR = $7B, so the
        sta w16                     ; adc above cannot carry, and the copy loop leaves C
argument: Both `clc`s are dead. Path changed: the whole body of bar_digit after the BARCACHE miss, i.e. once per HUD digit whose value actually changed -- it is the only path through these lines. (1) `stza ptr+1` (logic.s 3055) zeroes ptr+1, so before the second `rol ptr+1` that byte holds 0 or 1; rol shifts its bit 7 into C, and bit 7 of 0 or 1 is 0. C is therefore 0 at the first clc for every possible X, with no range assumption. (2) After that, A = ((x & $FE) * 4) & $FF, and `adc #<BARADDR` with C = 0 cannot set C either, because BARADDR = RINGBASE + RINGBYTES = $3500 + $4600 = $7B00, so #<BARADDR = 0 and the low add is a no-op. `lda ptr+1 / adc #>BARADDR` then adds at most 3 + $7B + 0 = $7E, so it too leaves C = 0, and the 32-byte copy loop (lda (zp),y / sta (zp),y / dey / bpl) touches no carry -- so the second clc is redundant as well. Flags: the removed clc's only consumer was the adc that follows it; N/Z after the sequence are identical, and the next consumer is `bpl :-` in the loop, long after. 4 cycles and 2 bytes per changed digit. The `add16i ptr, 640` further down keeps its clc -- C there is 1 on the `inc w16+1` path -- and no anonymous label is added or removed.

original:

        lsr                         ; C = d bit0, A = d >> 1
        sta w16+1
        lda #0
        ror                         ; A = d0 << 7
        lsr w16+1                   ; C = d bit1, w16+1 = d >> 2
        ror                         ; A = d1 << 7 | d0 << 6
        clc
        adc #<SPR_DIGITS
        sta w16
        lda w16+1
        adc #>SPR_DIGITS
        sta w16+1                   ; digit tile
        txa
        and #$FE                    ; char = x/2, then *8 -- i.e. (x & $FE) * 4
        stza ptr+1
        asl
        rol ptr+1
        asl
        rol ptr+1
        clc
        adc #<BARADDR               ; straight into the back buffer's bar row (no offscreen
        sta ptr                     ; buffer): bank 4 glyph at $8xxx, screen bar at $7Bxx
        lda ptr+1
        adc #>BARADDR

proposal:
pla
        lsr                         ; C = d bit0, A = d >> 1
        sta w16+1
        lda #0
        ror                         ; A = d0 << 7
        lsr w16+1                   ; C = d bit1, w16+1 = d >> 2
        ror                         ; A = d1 << 7 | d0 << 6, C = 0 (bit0 of d0<<7)
        adc #<SPR_DIGITS
        sta w16
        lda w16+1
        adc #>SPR_DIGITS
        sta w16+1                   ; digit tile
        txa
        and #$FE                    ; char = x/2, then *8 -- i.e. (x & $FE) * 4
        stza ptr+1
        asl
        rol ptr+1
        asl
        rol ptr+1                   ; ptr+1 <= 3, so this rol leaves C = 0
        adc #<BARADDR               ; straight into the back buffer's bar row (no offscreen
        sta ptr                     ; buffer): bank 4 glyph at $8xxx, screen bar at $7Bxx
        lda ptr+1
        adc #>BARADDR
        sta ptr+1
argument: Both clc instructions are provably redundant; there is no label between them and the code that sets carry, so no other path enters. (1) First clc. A is loaded with lda #0, then ror A rotates C=d bit0 in, giving A = d0<<7 and leaving C = bit0 of the old A = bit0 of $00 = 0. lsr w16+1 then overwrites C with d bit1 but does not touch A. The second ror A gives A = d1<<7|d0<<6 and leaves C = bit0 of its operand, which was d0<<7 -- bit0 of that is 0. So C is 0 entering adc #<SPR_DIGITS. (2) Second clc. stza ptr+1 zeroes ptr+1 (stz sets no flags). asl A sets C from A bit7; rol ptr+1 shifts 0 left, so it leaves C = bit7 of $00 = 0 and ptr+1 in {0,1}. asl A again sets C; the second rol ptr+1 leaves C = bit7 of a value that is 0 or 1, i.e. 0, and ptr+1 <= 3. So C is 0 entering adc #<BARADDR. Removing each clc saves 2 cycles and 1 byte; the adc results, and hence every later flag and value, are identical. Path: this is the body of bar_digit after the BARCACHE miss, i.e. every HUD digit that actually changed value (the cache-hit path exits at bd_same before reaching these lines). 4 cycles per redrawn digit, both buffers.

assumption: X still equals SECIDX at this point (irq_handler does `ldx SECIDX` at engine.s:2914 and nothing between there and here touches X or SECIDX -- the intervening code is only lda SECTAB+n,x / sta CRTC_* pairs), and X is dead after the store (@exit at engine.s:3027-3031 does `ldy irq_y / ldx irq_x / lda $FC / rti`).
original:
lda SECTAB+4,x
        beq @stay
        txa
        clc
        adc #8
        tax
@stay:  stx SECIDX
        jmp @exit
proposal:
lda SECTAB+4,x
        beq @stay
        txa
        clc
        adc #8
        sta SECIDX                  ; X is dead: @exit restores it from irq_x
@stay:  jmp @exit                   ; X is still SECIDX here, so nothing to store
argument:
Two independent facts, both checked in engine.s. (a) X is reloaded from irq_x at @exit, so X need not carry the new index -- the `tax` exists only to feed `stx SECIDX`, and storing A directly with `sta SECIDX` (SECIDX is in the TABLES segment, so abs: 4 cycles, 3 bytes, the same as `stx SECIDX`) removes the `tax` outright. (b) X was loaded from SECIDX on entry to the T1 arm and is unchanged, so on the @stay path SECIDX already holds exactly the value `stx SECIDX` would write; the store is a no-op and can go, leaving @stay as the label on the `jmp @exit`.

Costs. Advance path (SECTAB+4,x != 0): was txa 2 + clc 2 + adc 2 + tax 2 + stx 4 = 12, now txa 2 + clc 2 + adc 2 + sta 4 = 10, saving 2. Stay path (SECTAB+4,x == 0): was stx 4 + jmp 3 = 7, now jmp 3, saving 4. Bytes: tax (1) + stx abs (3) = 4 replaced by sta abs (3), saving 1.

Which path, how often: this is the T1 (rupture-chain) arm of irq_handler, taken once per section per frame. The chain advances on every section except Q -- the one entry with R6 = 0 -- so the advance path (2 cycles) is the common one, taken on every T1 IRQ but the last of the frame, and the stay path (4 cycles) once per frame. I quote 2 as the saving because that is the value on the busy path.

Correctness: no flags are consumed after the store (`jmp @exit`, then ldy/ldx/lda/rti, and rti restores P from the stack), so the difference between `sta`'s no flags and `stx`'s no flags is moot -- both are flag-free anyway. No anonymous labels are added or removed; @stay is a named local label and its only reference is the `beq @stay` two lines above. A is dead at @exit (`lda $FC` reloads it).

assumption: X is dead after 'stx SECIDX': @exit does 'ldy irq_y / ldx irq_x / lda $FC / rti', so X is reloaded from irq_x before the rti (engine.s:3027-3031). SECIDX is in the TABLES segment, so stx/sta to it is absolute (4 cycles).
original:
lda SECTAB+4,x
        beq @stay
        txa
        clc
        adc #8
        tax
@stay:  stx SECIDX
        jmp @exit
proposal:
lda SECTAB+4,x
        beq @stay
        txa
        clc
        adc #8
        sta SECIDX
        jmp @exit
@stay:  stx SECIDX
        jmp @exit
argument: Path changed: the 'chain advances' arm, taken on every T1 rupture IRQ except the last section of the frame (the chain runs T -> [A] -> P.. -> [P2] -> Q, so 4-5 T1 IRQs a frame and all but the Q one advance). Original on that arm: lda abs,x 4, beq not taken 2, txa 2, clc 2, adc #8 2, tax 2, stx SECIDX (abs) 4 = 18, then jmp 3. The 'tax' exists only so that the shared 'stx SECIDX' can store the new index; X itself is dead because @exit restores it from irq_x. Storing A directly with 'sta SECIDX' (abs, 4) drops the tax, so the arm costs 16 + jmp, a saving of 2 cycles. The @stay arm is left byte-for-byte identical (lda 4, beq taken 3, stx 4) and is unchanged in cost. Cost: the @stay arm now needs its own 'jmp @exit', +3 bytes. No anonymous labels are involved (@stay is a named cheap-local label), and no flags are consumed after either store. Net per frame roughly 4 x 2 = 8 cycles off the most latency-critical handler in the program.

assumption: w16b is dead on exit from @addr. Verified: every reference to w16b between engine.s:2391 and engine.s:2411 is inside @addr itself, and the three callers (@emit, the P2 block, @setq) go straight on to tmp2/tmp3/SECTAB work. w16 itself is unchanged by both versions, as before.
original:
@addr:  lda w16
        sta w16b
        lda w16+1
        sta w16b+1
        cmp #>(RINGCHARS-ROWCHARS+1)
        bcc :++
        bne :+
        lda w16b
        cmp #<(RINGCHARS-ROWCHARS+1)
        bcc :++
:       lda w16b
        sec
        sbc #<RINGCHARS
        sta w16b
        lda w16b+1
        sbc #>RINGCHARS
        sta w16b+1
:       lda w16b
        clc
        adc #<CRTCBASE
        tay
        lda w16b+1
        adc #>CRTCBASE
        sta SECTAB,x
        tya
        sta SECTAB+1,x
        rts
proposal:
@addr:  lda w16+1
        cmp #>(RINGCHARS-ROWCHARS+1)
        bcc :++
        bne :+
        lda w16
        cmp #<(RINGCHARS-ROWCHARS+1)
        bcc :++
:       lda w16                     ; straddles the ring end: -RINGCHARS folded
        clc                         ; into the CRTCBASE add, so no w16b copy at all
        adc #<((CRTCBASE-RINGCHARS) & $FFFF)
        tay
        lda w16+1
        adc #>((CRTCBASE-RINGCHARS) & $FFFF)
        sta SECTAB,x
        tya
        sta SECTAB+1,x
        rts
:       lda w16
        clc
        adc #<CRTCBASE
        tay
        lda w16+1
        adc #>CRTCBASE
        sta SECTAB,x
        tya
        sta SECTAB+1,x
        rts
argument: @addr currently copies w16 into w16b, conditionally subtracts RINGCHARS from w16b, then adds CRTCBASE to w16b. The subtraction and the addition are both exact mod 65536 (the intermediate sta w16b is 8-bit but the borrow/carry propagates), so (w16 - RINGCHARS) + CRTCBASE is identical to w16 + (CRTCBASE - RINGCHARS). Folding them removes the w16b scratch entirely and lets both arms read w16 directly, one arm adding CRTCBASE and the other adding (CRTCBASE-RINGCHARS). CRTCBASE = $3500/8 = $06A0 and RINGCHARS = 80*28 = $08C0, so CRTCBASE-RINGCHARS = -544; masking with $FFFF makes it $FDE0, whose #< is $E0 and #> is $FD (checked: 2200 + $FDE0 mod 65536 = 1656 = 2200-2240+1696). The 16-bit unsigned test against RINGCHARS-ROWCHARS+1 is copied unchanged, only now reading w16/w16+1 instead of the just-written w16b copy. Anonymous labels: the original has exactly two ':' lines in this block and so does the proposal, in the same order (first = wrap, second = no-wrap), so bcc :++ / bne :+ / bcc :++ still name the same targets and no branch elsewhere is retargeted; forward displacements are +24, +6 and +18, all in range. Exit state matches the original exactly: A = low byte, Y = low byte, X untouched, flags from the final tya, C from the final adc. Path changed and its frequency: the no-wrap arm, taken whenever w16 < RINGCHARS-ROWCHARS+1, i.e. for about 2160 of 2240 ring offsets (~96% of calls). Old cost on that arm 49 cycles (3+3+3+3+2+3 prologue, then 3+2+2+2+3+2+5+2+5+6), new cost 40 (3+2+3, then 3+2+2+2+3+2+5+2+5+6) = 9 cycles saved; the hi==$08 sub-case saves the same 9 (58 -> 49). The rare wrap arm saves 27 (69 -> 42). Bytes 51 -> 50.

original:
lda O_XL,y                  ; rx/ry = object relative to the player
        sec
        sbc px
        sta rx
        lda O_XH,y
        sta spx+1                   ; sta touches no flags, so C survives for the sbc
        sbc px+1
        sta rx+1
        lda O_YL,y
        sta spy
        sec
        sbc py
        sta ry
        lda O_YH,y
        sbc py+1
        sta ry+1
        lda O_XL,y                  ; spx/spy = where it draws
        sta spx
        lda O_YH,y
        sta spy+1
proposal:
lda O_XL,y                  ; rx/ry = object relative to the player
        sta spx                     ; spx/spy come from the same loads: sta sets no flags
        sec
        sbc px
        sta rx
        lda O_XH,y
        sta spx+1                   ; sta touches no flags, so C survives for the sbc
        sbc px+1
        sta rx+1
        lda O_YL,y
        sta spy
        sec
        sbc py
        sta ry
        lda O_YH,y
        sta spy+1
        sbc py+1
        sta ry+1
argument: The block already uses this trick for two of the four bytes: O_XH is stored to spx+1 between its load and the sbc, and O_YL to spy between its load and the sec/sbc, precisely because sta sets no flags and so does not disturb the borrow chain. The same holds for the other two bytes, which are instead re-loaded at the end. Moving sta spx to immediately after lda O_XL,y is safe: sta sets no flags, so the following sec/sbc px is unaffected, and nothing between that point and the old lda O_XL,y writes spx. Moving sta spy+1 to between lda O_YH,y and sbc py+1 is safe for the same reason, and C there is the borrow out of sbc py, which sta does not touch; nothing in between writes spy+1. That makes the trailing lda O_XL,y and lda O_YH,y dead, and they are deleted. O_XL/O_YH are absolute tables (O_XL = LV_OBJST + 2*OBJN etc.), so each removed load is lda abs,y = 4 cycles / 3 bytes: 8 cycles and 6 bytes, or 10 cycles when both indexed reads happen to cross a page. Y is unchanged throughout (it is the object index and no instruction here touches it), so the two remaining indexed loads still address the same object. A is left holding ry+1 instead of spy+1, and the next instruction is lda otype, so no flag or register state is carried past the block. This is the @lean prologue of process_object, executed once for every object whose type is below NLEAN on every frame -- the only path through this half of the window (the fd/fe store-back above it belongs to the staged path and is not touched).

assumption: ox/oy/spx/spy/rx/ry/px/py/fa..fe are distinct zero-page locations (verified: ox=$A8, oy=$AA, fa=$AC..fe=$B4, rx=$B6, ry=$B8 in logic.s; px/py and spx/spy are separate reservations), and nothing between @gen and the dispatch reads spx/spy/rx/ry. Y must stay the object index throughout, which it already does.
original:

        sta ox
        lda O_XH,y
        sta ox+1
        lda O_YL,y
        sta oy
        lda O_YH,y
        sta oy+1
        lda O_AL,y
        sta fa
        lda O_AH,y
        sta fa+1

Flags/registers: the original ends with sta t16+1 and so does the proposal, and the very next instruction is bge16's lda fb, which re-derives everything it needs (it sets C itself via cmp), so neither the leftover carry from adc nor A matters. X and Y are untouched by both. No anonymous label is added or removed (mov16 and add16i contain none; bge16's single ':' is unchanged). Path changed and frequency: the @c4 arm of ob_snake's fc dispatch (fc = 4, the 'drift right' state), one of four arms reached per snake per frame from @st; @coll below it is common to all arms and is unchanged. So this is 12 cycles on roughly one snake update in four, not 12 on every snake. It is a leftover of exactly the mov16+add16i fusion pattern already applied elsewhere in this file (see the comment at logic.s:2663).

original:
mov16 t16, fa
        add16i t16, 128
        bge16 fb, t16, @coll
proposal:
lda fa
        clc
        adc #<128
        sta t16
        lda fa+1
        adc #>128
        sta t16+1

argument: A surviving mov16+add16i pair. mov16 t16, fa expands to lda fa / sta t16 / lda fa+1 / sta t16+1 (12 cycles, 8 bytes, all zero page: fa = $AC, t16 = $D1). add16i t16, 128 then expands to clc / lda t16 / adc #<128 / sta t16 / lda t16+1 / adc #>128 / sta t16+1 (2+3+2+3+3+2+3 = 18 cycles, 13 bytes). Total 30 cycles, 21 bytes. The fused form reads fa directly instead of reading back what was just written to t16: lda fa (3) / clc (2) / adc #<128 (2) / sta t16 (3) / lda fa+1 (3) / adc #>128 (2) / sta t16+1 (3) = 18 cycles, 13 bytes. 128 = $0080 so #<128 = $80 and #>128 = $00, and the carry out of the low byte still propagates into the high byte exactly as before -- t16 = fa + 128 in both versions, with identical wraparound. The clc is kept because the carry state on entry to @c4 is unknown (the dispatch above arrives via 'cmp #4 / beq @c4'). Flags after the sequence: both versions end with adc then sta, and sta sets no flags, so N,V,Z,C are the same in both. X and Y are untouched by both. No anonymous labels are added or removed. assumption: X is dead across the pha/pla region. Verified: no instruction between them reads or writes X (mov16i and stza with one argument are A-only, stz anim is unindexed, there is no jsr), and after @acc the next reference to X anywhere on the path is inside `jsr getaltitude` at @hget, which loads its own.

        beq :+
        bpl @acc288

@acc288:

@acc:   pla

tax
        lda running
        ora firing
        bne :+
        stz anim
:       ; accel = (alt > 0 || push == 3) ? 288 : 36

        beq :+
        bpl @acc288

Flags: pha sets none but the next instruction is `lda running`, which overwrites N and Z, so tax's flag side effect is harmless; pla sets N,Z from the popped byte and txa sets N,Z from the identical byte, and in any case the next instruction `and #K_LEFT` recomputes them. assumption: On this (downward) path dpx+1 is always 0, so clamping when dpx == alt is a no-op and skipping it is equivalent. vy_step (logic.s:1205) leaves dpx+1 as exactly 0 or $FF, and 'bmi16 dpx, @up' immediately above diverts the $FF case to @up, so dpx+1 = 0 here. alt is a single byte (alt = $C2, q1 = $C3).
original:
lda dpx
        cmp alt
        bcc :+
        lda alt
        sta dpx
        stz dpx+1
:       add16 py, dpx
        lda alt
        sec
        sbc dpx
        sta alt
proposal:
lda alt
        cmp dpx
        bcs :+
        sta dpx
        stz dpx+1
:       sec
        sbc dpx
        sta alt
        add16 py, dpx
argument: Reversing the compare operands lets A hold alt at the merge point on both arms, which kills two 'lda zp'. Original: 'lda dpx / cmp alt / bcc skip' clamps when dpx >= alt, and on the clamp arm reloads alt into A ('lda alt / sta dpx'); after add16 it reloads alt a third time for 'alt -= dpx'. New: 'lda alt / cmp dpx / bcs skip' skips when alt >= dpx; on the clamp arm A already holds alt so 'sta dpx' needs no load, and at the merge point A holds alt on both arms (clamp arm: A = alt from the load; skip arm: A = alt from the same load), so 'sec / sbc dpx / sta alt' runs with no reload. 'add16 py, dpx' is moved after the alt update - it starts with its own clc so the borrow state does not matter, it does not read alt, and the alt update does not read or write py or dpx, so the two are independent. The only behavioural difference is at dpx == alt: the original clamps (dpx := alt, a no-op on the low byte, plus stz dpx+1) and the new form skips; with dpx+1 = 0 guaranteed by vy_step both are identical. Both comparisons are unsigned, as before. The anonymous-label count is unchanged (one ':' before, one after), so no ':+'/':++' elsewhere is retargeted. Cycles, common path (dpx < alt, i.e. free fall with headroom - the usual case every frame): old 3+3+3 then 20 for add16 then 3+2+3+3 = 40; new 3+3+3 then 2+3+3 then 20 = 37, saving 3. Clamped path (the landing frame): old 48, new 42, saving 6. Bytes 32 -> 28. Path: player_update's downward vertical step, executed once per frame.

original:
@draw:  ble16i fb, -128, @done
        mov16 t16, fa
        add16i t16, 128
        bge16 fb, t16, @done

        clc

argument: `mov16 t16, fa` (lda fa / sta t16 / lda fa+1 / sta t16+1, 12 cycles, 8 bytes) followed by `add16i t16, 128` (clc / lda t16 / adc #128 / sta t16 / lda t16+1 / adc #0 / sta t16+1, 18 cycles, 13 bytes) stages the copy through t16 only to read it straight back.  Adding into t16 from fa directly gives the identical 16-bit result t16 = fa + 128 in 18 cycles and 13 bytes -- the copy vanishes entirely.  fa/fa+1 are zero page ($AC), same addressing cost as t16.  Flags: both versions end with `sta t16+1` preceded by `adc #0`, and the next instruction is bge16's `lda fb`, so N/Z/C are dead.  No anonymous label is added or removed (neither macro contains one; ble16i and bge16 keep their own, untouched).  The `original` is extended by one line either side because the identical two-line pair also occurs at logic.s:2224 (@c4 in the same file) and would otherwise be ambiguous to a string match.  This is ob_snake's @draw fall-through, executed once per snake per frame whenever fb > -128, i.e. essentially every frame the snake exists -- the window's hot path.

original:
@draw:  ble16i fb, -128, @done
        mov16 t16, fa
        add16i t16, 128
        bge16 fb, t16, @done
proposal:
@draw:  ble16i fb, -128, @done
        clc
        lda fa
        adc #128
        sta t16
        lda fa+1
        adc #0
        sta t16+1
        bge16 fb, t16, @done
argument: A mov16/add16i fusion that survived round 1, presumably because a 16-instruction window cut between the two macros. 'mov16 t16, fa' expands to lda fa / sta t16 / lda fa+1 / sta t16+1 (12 cycles, 8 bytes) and 'add16i t16, 128' to clc / lda t16 / adc #<128 / sta t16 / lda t16+1 / adc #>128 / sta t16+1 (18 cycles, 13 bytes): 30 cycles, 21 bytes. Nothing reads t16 between the two, so the add can read fa directly -- clc / lda fa / adc #128 / sta t16 / lda fa+1 / adc #0 / sta t16+1 is 18 cycles and 13 bytes, saving 12 cycles and 8 bytes. Note #<128 = 128 and #>128 = 0, so the immediates are 128 and 0 exactly as add16i would have emitted them. No aliasing: fa = $AC (logic.s:255, 2 bytes since fb = $AE), t16 = $D1 (logic.s:282). t16 ends with the same value and the same carry from the high 'adc', and the next instruction is bge16's 'lda fb' which sets its own flags, so the flag state is irrelevant either way. Path: the single fall-through path of the @draw block, reached on every ob_snake tick whose fb is greater than -128 -- i.e. essentially every frame for every live snake; it is the block's only path, the surrounding code is all early-outs to @done.

assumption: X is dead at @afterhurt and t16 is dead after this compare. Both are visible: the hurt block immediately above only loads X when hurt != 0, so nothing downstream can already depend on X; @noctl's first act is 'ldx vx+1'; and the next reference to t16 anywhere in player_update after this point is a write (the bullet-velocity 'sta t16'), never a read.
original:
@afterhurt:
        lda control
        bne @ctl
        lda frame
        sec
        sbc evframe
        sta t16
        lda frame+1
        sbc evframe+1
        bne @setctl
        lda t16
        cmp #25
        bcc @noctl
proposal:
@afterhurt:
        lda control
        bne @ctl
        lda frame
        sec
        sbc evframe
        tax                         ; hold the low byte of the delta in X
        lda frame+1
        sbc evframe+1
        bne @setctl
        cpx #25
        bcc @noctl
argument: This is the same unsigned 16-bit elapsed-frames test as the hurt block eight lines above, which already parks the delta's low byte in X and finishes with cpx #65; the control-timeout copy below it still stages through t16. Replacing sta t16 (3 cycles, 2 bytes) with tax (2 cycles, 1 byte) and lda t16 / cmp #25 (5 cycles, 4 bytes) with cpx #25 (3 cycles, 2 bytes) saves 3 cycles and 3 bytes. Correctness: tax, like sta, leaves C untouched, so the borrow from 'sbc evframe' still reaches 'sbc evframe+1' and the 'bne @setctl' still reads the high-byte result's Z; cpx is an unsigned compare setting C exactly as cmp did, so 'bcc @noctl' is unchanged. The only behavioural difference is A at the fall-through into @setctl -- formerly the delta low byte, now the high byte -- and @setctl's first instruction is 'lda #1', so A is dead there. No anonymous labels are involved. Path: the block runs only when control = 0, i.e. during the post-death freeze until the 25-frame timeout re-enables control, once per frame for roughly 25 frames per death -- so this is a byte-and-tidiness win with a small cycle rider, not a per-frame saving.

assumption: X is unchanged between the 'tax' that follows 'sta bent' (two instructions above the quoted block) and 'beq @skip': the intervening 'lda LV_BOBJ,x', 'tay', 'lda frame' and 'cmp O_STAMP,y' read X but never write it. Verified in logic.s lines 995-1002.
original:

        cmp O_STAMP,y
        beq @skip
        sta O_STAMP,y
        lda O_TYPE,y
        bne @apo                    ; that, so a cached step and a rebuilt one take the
        ldx NSTARL                  ; same path through the handlers.  Stars go in their
        cpx #BINMAX                 ; own list: the walk then reaches ob_star without
        bcs @full                   ; reading the type or going through the table.
        tya
        sta LV_BINSTAR,x
        inc NSTARL
        bra @skip
@apo:   ldx NOTHL
        cpx #BINMAX
        bcs @full
        tya
        sta LV_BINOTH,x
        inc NOTHL
        bra @skip
@full:  stz BINOK                   ; more objects than a list holds: process this one
        sty obj                     ; now and rebuild next step rather than lose it
        jsr process_object
        setbank BANK_LVL
@skip:  ldx bent
        lda LV_BNEXT,x

lda frame
        cmp O_STAMP,y
        beq @sk2                    ; already stamped: X is still bent, skip the reload
        sta O_STAMP,y
        lda O_TYPE,y
        bne @apo                    ; that, so a cached step and a rebuilt one take the
        ldx NSTARL                  ; same path through the handlers.  Stars go in their
        cpx #BINMAX                 ; own list: the walk then reaches ob_star without
        bcs @full                   ; reading the type or going through the table.
        tya
        sta LV_BINSTAR,x
        inc NSTARL
        bra @skip
@apo:   ldx NOTHL
        cpx #BINMAX
        bcs @full
        tya
        sta LV_BINOTH,x
        inc NOTHL
        bra @skip
@full:  stz BINOK                   ; more objects than a list holds: process this one
        sty obj                     ; now and rebuild next step rather than lose it
        jsr process_object
        setbank BANK_LVL
@skip:  ldx bent
@sk2:   lda LV_BNEXT,x
        bra @walk
argument: Path changed: the 'beq @skip' arm -- an object whose O_STAMP already equals frame, i.e. the second and later times the same object is met while walking the grid-cell lists during a bin rebuild. On that arm X still holds bent (set by the 'tax' right after 'sta bent'), so '@skip: ldx bent' reloads a value X already has. Splitting the join point one instruction later -- 'beq @sk2' with '@skip: ldx bent' falling into '@sk2: lda LV_BNEXT,x' -- saves the 3-cycle 'ldx bent' (bent = $CF, zero page). The other three ways into @skip still need it: the star arm leaves X = NSTARL, the other arm X = NOTHL, and the @full arm has been through jsr process_object; all three still enter at @skip and reload. Frequency: an object is linked into every grid cell it overlaps, so objects that straddle a cell boundary are visited 2-4 times and only the first visit does work -- the already-stamped arm is a large share of all visits (scene-dependent, but comparable to the star/other arms combined). Correctness: X is the only thing the new entry point depends on; A holds frame and Y holds the object index on both paths, and LV_BNEXT,x is a load so no flags are carried in. Bytes unchanged (a cheap label costs nothing); branch range is fine, @sk2 is only ~58 bytes forward. No anonymous labels are involved -- both labels are ca65 cheap locals, and '@sk2' is unused elsewhere in game_frame's scope.

assumption: addsprite does not read q1 or the incoming carry: it is 'ldx NSPR / cpx #MAXSPR / ...' (engine.s:997) and takes only A plus spx/spy, and m_addsprite is TOMAIN "addsprite" (jsr addsprite / jmp pagelogic).
proposal:
@f2:    lda fc
        and #1
        ora #46+2                   ; base is even, so ora == the old clc/adc
        jmp m_addsprite
@f0:    lda fc
        and #1
        ora #46+0
        jmp m_addsprite
@f4:    lda fc
        and #1
        ora #46+4
        jmp m_addsprite
@f6:    lda fc
        and #1
        ora #46+6
        jmp m_addsprite
argument: Path changed: the sprite-id tail of ob_snake's @draw, run once per live snake per logic step; the three fe arms (@f0/@f2/@f4) reach it via 'bra @fr' and the fc>=2 arm (@f6) falls into it. The tail is q1 = base; A = (fc & 1) + q1. Two observations: the bases 46, 48, 50, 52 are all even and fc & 1 is 0 or 1, so 'clc / adc q1' is exactly 'ora #base' -- and once the add is an immediate ora, q1 and the branch to the shared tail both disappear. Old cost for an fe arm: lda #imm 2 + bra @fr 3 + sta q1 3 + lda fc 3 + and #1 2 + clc 2 + adc q1 3 + jmp 3 = 21; new: lda fc 3 + and #1 2 + ora #imm 2 + jmp 3 = 10, so 11 cycles. The @f6 arm fell through rather than branching, so it saves 8. Correctness: 'lda fc' reads the low byte of the 16-bit fc exactly as before; the result is identical bit for bit because base bit 0 is clear; q1 is a scratch temp with no other reader in ob_snake (grep: q1 appears only in this tail). The flags handed to m_addsprite change (ora leaves C from the cmp chain instead of the cleared C from adc), which is why the assumption above matters -- addsprite's first instruction pair is ldx/cpx, which overwrites C before anything reads it. @fr is removed and is referenced only by the three bra lines being replaced; @f0/@f2/@f4/@f6 keep their labels, and every branch into them (bcs @f6, bcc @f0/@f2/@f4) stays well inside range. Cost: +10 bytes for the four copies of the tail -- cycles first, but this is a low-frequency routine, so if bytes are tight the strictly-smaller subset of this change is to leave the block alone and only swap 'clc / adc q1' for 'ora q1' (2 cycles, -1 byte).

assumption: On the `beq :++` arm X now holds maplw (8) instead of its previous value. Nothing on that arm reads X before redefining it: it runs `lda #1 / sta t16b+1`, then the merge point `lda t16b / sta MAPSTRIDE / lda t16b+1 / sta MAPSTRIDE+1`, then `ldx #0`.
original:
lda maplw
        cmp #8
        beq :++
        lda #1
        ldx maplw
:       asl
        dex
        bne :-
proposal:
ldx maplw
        cpx #8
        beq :++
        lda #1
:       asl
        dex
        bne :-
argument: maplw is loaded twice: once into A purely to compare it against 8, and once into X to drive the shift counter. Doing the compare with `cpx` off the X copy removes the A load entirely. `cpx #8` sets Z from maplw-8 exactly as `cmp #8` did, so `beq :++` behaves identically; `lda #1` after the branch sets A and does not disturb X; the `: asl / dex / bne :-` loop is untouched and still sees X = maplw. Neither `:` line is added or removed, so the anonymous-label count is unchanged. Cycles: lda zp 3 + cmp #imm 2 + lda #imm 2 + ldx zp 3 = 10 becomes ldx zp 3 + cpx #imm 2 + lda #imm 2 = 7. Bytes: 8 -> 6. Path: the entry path of init_maprows, executed once per level load (level_init's first instruction is `jsr init_maprows`), so the cycle figure is negligible -- the two bytes are the real point in a segment the file describes as full.

original:
cmp #BUFROWS+1
        bcc :+
        lda #BUFROWS
        sec
        sbc tmp
        beq @none
        bmi @none
        sta rc_h
proposal:
cmp #BUFROWS+1
        bcc :+
        lda #BUFROWS                ; bcc not taken: C = 1 already, for the sbc
        sbc tmp
        beq @none
        bmi @none
        sta rc_h
argument: lda #BUFROWS is reachable only by falling through the bcc :+ immediately above it -- it is not a branch target and nothing jumps into it. Falling through means the branch was not taken, which means C = 1 from cmp #BUFROWS+1, and lda #imm affects only N and Z, not C. The sec is therefore a no-op and can be deleted: 2 cycles, 1 byte. The codebase already relies on exactly this reasoning twice in the same routine (bcs @none ; not taken: C = 0 for the adc, and bcc :+ ; not taken: C = 1 for the sbc in the column clip below), so the idiom is established; this instance was simply missed. Flags after are unchanged: sbc tmp still produces the same N and Z for the beq/bmi pair and the same difference for sta rc_h. Path: this is the bottom-clip arm of the row clip in drawrect_clip, taken only when the rect's last row runs past BUFROWS; the common case branches over it at the bcc, so the saving applies only to clipped rects and is worth 2 cycles each time one occurs -- small, but free and risk-free.

original:
lda bounce
        beq :+
        mov16i vy, -1280
proposal:
lda bounce
        beq :+
        stz vy
        lda #>(-1280)
        sta vy+1
argument:
Path changed: the bounce arm in game_frame, taken only on frames where `bounce` is non-zero (the player has just landed on a bouncy tile) - a small minority of frames; the dominant path through this window is the `beq :+` fall-through, which is untouched. The value here is really the byte, not the cycles.
-1280 = $FB00, so `mov16i vy, -1280` expands to `lda #<(-1280)` = `lda #$00` (2), `sta vy` (3), `lda #>(-1280)` = `lda #$FB` (2), `sta vy+1` (3) = 10 cycles / 8 bytes. Because the low byte of the immediate is zero, the first two instructions are exactly `stz vy` (3 cycles / 2 bytes, vy is zero page), giving 8 cycles / 7 bytes.
The high byte is written with `#>(-1280)` (= $FB), not `#<`, and the store order is unchanged.
State at the join: both forms leave A = $FB with N=1,Z=0 from the `lda #>(-1280)`; `stz` on a 65C02 sets no flags, so the flag state at `:` is identical to before. The next instruction after `:` is `lda health`, so neither A nor the flags are live anyway. No anonymous labels are added or removed (mov16i contains none, and neither does the replacement).

assumption: @fell is referenced only by this branch (grep of logic.s confirms line 1326 is its only reference), so it may become a fall-through label.
proposal:
bge16 t16, py, @push
@fell:  mov16 evframe, frame
argument:
Path changed: the fall-through (not-fallen) arm of the maph-24 death test in player_update, which runs once per frame and is taken on essentially every frame (the @fell arm runs once per death).
bgt16 aa,bb,label expands to `lda bb / cmp aa / lda bb+1 / sbc aa+1 / bvc :+ / eor #$80 / : bmi label`, so `bgt16 py, t16, @fell` computes t16 - py and branches on N (after V correction) i.e. when py > t16.
bge16 aa,bb,label expands to `lda aa / cmp bb / lda aa+1 / sbc bb+1 / bvc :+ / eor #$80 / : bpl label`, so `bge16 t16, py, @push` computes the SAME subtraction t16 - py and branches on the complementary condition t16 >= py, i.e. exactly when the old code fell through to `bra @push`. The two conditions are exact complements, so the two arms are preserved and @fell is reached by fall-through.
Both macro bodies are instruction-for-instruction identical in cost and both contain exactly one anonymous `:` label, so the anonymous-label count through this routine is unchanged and no `:+`/`:-` elsewhere is retargeted.
Cycles, @push arm: old = bmi not taken (2) + bra (3) = 5; new = bpl taken (3) = 3, saving 2. @fell arm: old = bmi taken (3); new = bpl not taken (2), saving 1. Even with a page-crossing taken branch (4) the new form is never worse: old min 5, new max 4. Bytes: the 2-byte `bra` disappears.
Flags/registers: both forms leave A = (t16+1 - py+1) possibly EORed with $80 and C from the sbc; the next instruction on either arm is `mov16 evframe, frame` or `mov16 qx, px`, both of which begin with an `lda`, so neither A nor the flags are live across the branch.
Verified: a patched copy of the tree assembles cleanly under ca65 --cpu 65C02 and links, with the segment shrinking by exactly the predicted byte count.

assumption: facing is only ever 0 or 1 (set by stz facing at logic.s 839/1173/1449 and lda #1/sta facing at 1446), and every value that reaches @sprf is even: 8/10/12 from @standing, 20/22/24 from @jump, 14/16/18 from the @ctl firing arm, and 'lda anim / lsr / and #$FE' from @ground. The odd id 23 enters at @spr, below the add.
original:
@sprf:  clc
        adc facing
proposal: @sprf:  ora facing
argument: Every sprite base id arriving at @sprf has bit 0 clear and facing contributes only bit 0, so the add can never carry into bit 1 and ora computes the identical result. That replaces clc (2) + adc facing (4, facing is an absolute .res byte) with ora facing (4): 2 cycles and 1 byte. Flags are not consumed -- the next instruction is 'tax' and then 'lda hurt', which resets N/Z -- and ora leaves A with the same value, so @spr is unaffected. The odd-id entry at @spr2 (lda #23 / jmp @spr) bypasses @sprf entirely and is untouched. Path: @sprf is on every arm of the player sprite selection, so it runs once per player_update, i.e. once a frame. Only 2 cycles a frame -- correct and free, but small.

proposal:
bge16 t16, py, @push
@fell:  mov16 evframe, frame
argument: bgt16 py, t16, @fell expands to lda t16 / cmp py / lda t16+1 / sbc py+1 / bvc :+ / eor #$80 / : bmi @fell -- it branches when t16-py is signed-negative, i.e. py > t16. bge16 t16, py, @push expands to lda t16 / cmp py / lda t16+1 / sbc py+1 / bvc :+ / eor #$80 / : bpl @push -- the identical six instructions, with bmi replaced by bpl and the target swapped, branching when t16 >= py, which is exactly NOT(py > t16). So the fall-through now reaches @fell and the bra @push disappears. Both macros contain exactly one anonymous label, so the file-wide anonymous-label count is unchanged. @fell is referenced only at this one site (grep of logic.s: line 1326 is the sole use), so leaving the label in place unreferenced is harmless in ca65. Branch range: @push is ~32 bytes past the bpl, well inside a relative branch. Cost, normal path (player has not fallen out of the world, i.e. every frame but the death frame): was bmi not taken 2 + bra taken 3 = 5, now bpl taken 3 -- 2 cycles saved. On the death path: was bmi taken 3, now bpl not taken 2 -- 1 cycle. player_update runs once per frame, so this is 2 cycles a frame.

original:
; steps = (vx + 128) >> 8 ; dir = sign
        lda vx
        clc
        adc #128
        lda vx+1
        adc #0                      ; A = high byte of vx + 128
proposal:
; steps = (vx + 128) >> 8 ; dir = sign
        lda vx
        cmp #128
        lda vx+1
        adc #0                      ; A = high byte of vx + 128
argument: Only the carry out of the low-byte addition is wanted here: the sum itself is thrown away by the very next `lda vx+1`.  `clc` (2) + `adc #128` (2) sets C = 1 exactly when vx + 128 >= 256, i.e. when vx >= 128; `cmp #128` (2) sets C = 1 on exactly the same condition, so the `adc #0` that follows sees an identical carry and dpx gets the same value.  N and Z from the cmp are immediately overwritten by `lda vx+1`, and V is not read.  Saves 2 cycles and 1 byte (clc 1 + adc# 2 = 3 bytes becomes cmp# 2 bytes).  This is the unconditional fall-through at @hmove, reached once per player_update, i.e. once per frame, on every path through the window (the @acc288/@acc/@run arms above all converge here).  Note the same pattern is already fused in vy_step next door, which is why this one reads as a survivor rather than a deliberate choice.

assumption: @fr has no entry other than the three visible here: `bra @fr` from the #6 arm, `bra @fr` from @f2, and fall-through from @f4. Verified by grep -- @fr is a cheap-local label scoped to ob_walker and is referenced only at logic.s:2791 and 2795.

assumption: @fr is reached only from the three sites shown (the two 'bra @fr' and the fall-through from @f4) - verified, those are the only references to @fr in ob_walker.

        bcs @full                   ; not taken: C = 0 for the adc
        sta rc_h

The same complement-and-add idiom @dxpos uses eleven lines earlier does it in eor #$FF 2 + adc #BUFROWS 2 + adc wcy 3 + sta rc_y 3 = 10. Correctness: 'cmp #BUFROWS' fell through, so dy < 28 and C = 0; 'sta rc_h' changes no flags, so C is still 0 at the eor, and eor sets only N,Z. eor #$FF gives 255-dy, and with C=0 'adc #28' gives 283-dy, which for dy in 1..27 is always >= 256, so C comes out 1 and A = 27-dy; 'adc wcy' with C=1 then gives wcy+28-dy, identical to the old result including the mod-256 wrap (the old form also truncated at 'adc #BUFROWS'). rc_h is still stored for drawrect.
