I also looked at merging @full's tail into @dorows: it saves ~17 bytes but needs a 'bra @dorows' added to @dypos to keep the fall-through, which cancels the 'bra @done' it removes, so it is cycle-neutral on the busy path.

        bcs @full                   ; not taken: C = 0 for the adc
        sta rc_h
        lda wcy
        adc #BUFROWS
        sec
        sbc rc_h

proposal:

        bcs @full                   ; not taken: C = 0 for the adc
        sta rc_h
        eor #$FF                    ; A = 255 - rc_h, C still 0 from the cmp above
        adc #BUFROWS                ; A = BUFROWS-1-rc_h, C = 1 (rc_h <= BUFROWS-1)
        adc wcy                     ; + wcy + 1 -> wcy + BUFROWS - rc_h

argument:
Path changed: the @dypos arm of scroll_validate - a downward vertical scroll of 1..27 rows. scroll_validate runs once per frame; this arm is reached only when dy > 0 (the `@dyc: lda w16b / beq @done / bpl @dypos` test), i.e. on frames where the window scrolled down, which is a minority of frames but a common one in play. The @docols/@dyc/@full arms in this window are unchanged.
This applies exactly the trick the @dxpos arm three screens up already uses. On entry A = dy (= rc_h) and C = 0, guaranteed by the `cmp #BUFROWS` whose `bcs` was not taken (the existing comment states this). `sta rc_h` sets no flags, so C is still 0. `eor #$FF` gives 255 - dy and leaves C alone. `adc #BUFROWS` with C=0 gives 255 - dy + 28; since @dyc's `beq`/`bpl` guarantee 1 <= dy and the cmp guarantees dy <= 27, this is always >= 256, so C comes out 1 and A = BUFROWS-1-dy. `adc wcy` with C=1 then gives wcy + BUFROWS - dy, which is byte-for-byte the value the original computed as `(wcy + BUFROWS) - rc_h` (both are mod 256, and rc_y is an 8-bit field - @full and the @dyc negative arm also write it with a single `sta rc_y`).
rc_h is still written first and is not read again on this path, so dropping the `sbc rc_h` read is safe. C is left set rather than whatever the old `sbc` produced, but the fall-through at @dorows begins `lda wcx / sta rc_x`, so neither C nor A is live. No branches and no anonymous labels are involved.
Cycles: old `sta rc_h`(3) + `lda wcy`(3) + `adc #BUFROWS`(2) + `sec`(2) + `sbc rc_h`(3) + `sta rc_y`(3) = 16; new `sta rc_h`(3) + `eor #$FF`(2) + `adc #BUFROWS`(2) + `adc wcy`(3) + `sta rc_y`(3) = 13. Saving 3 cycles. Bytes: `lda wcy`(2) + `sec`(1) + `sbc rc_h`(2) = 5 out, `eor #$FF`(2) + `adc wcy`(2) = 4 in, so 1 byte. Verified by assembling a patched copy of the tree with ca65/ld65: clean assembly, CODE shrinks accordingly.

        lda #$FF                    ; range is clean once copied
        sta PART_LO,x

        clc
        adc wcx

Path changed: @go, which is the single join point of copy_partial - every call that gets past the `wfine == 0` and `nothing drawn` early exits passes through it exactly once, on both the @all arm and the incremental arm. copy_partial runs once per frame, so this is 3 cycles a frame.
A holds the first column to copy on arrival at @go (from `lda PART_LO,x / bra @go` or `lda #0`), and `sta tmp4` does not disturb A. The original then clobbers A with `lda #$FF` for the PART_LO/PART_HI writes and has to reload it with `lda tmp4` (3 cycles, 2 bytes). Simply moving the three PART_* instructions below the w16 computation lets the `clc / adc wcx` consume the A that is already live, and the reload disappears. That is the whole edit; nothing else changes.
Correctness: (a) `sta tmp4` sets no flags, so the `clc` immediately after it is still needed and still correct, and the carry chain into `lda wcx+1 / adc #0` is untouched; (b) the moved block only writes PART_LO,x and PART_HI,x and only reads X, and the w16 computation it moves past touches neither (it reads tmp4/wcx and writes w16), so the reorder is observationally identical; (c) X (= curbuf) is not modified by any instruction in the run, so `PART_LO,x` / `PART_HI,x` still index the same buffer; (d) tmp4 is still written before the later `lda tmp4` that builds ptr; (e) the PART_* stores still complete before `jsr ringaddr` (ringaddr, engine.s:351, does not touch PART_* in any case); (f) `stza PART_HI, x` is the stz macro, which never touches A on a 65C02, and `lda #$FF` is now the last thing to set A - but the next instruction after the run is `lda wcy`, so neither A nor the flags are live at the join.
Cycles: one `lda tmp4` (zero page) removed = 3. Bytes: 2.
Verified: a patched copy of the tree assembles cleanly under ca65 --cpu 65C02 and links, with the segment shrinking by exactly the predicted byte count.

proposal:

.endmacro
argument: blt16i and bge16i were already converted to the $8000-bias form, where the bias on the constant side is free at assembly time; ble16i and bgt16i were left on the old bvc/eor form. `var <= imm` is exactly `var < imm+1` in signed 16-bit, and imm is a literal at every call site, so imm+1 is folded by the assembler. Cost, with var in zero page: old = lda# 2 + cmp zp 3 + lda# 2 + sbc zp 3 = 10, then `bvc :+` 3 when V is clear (13 total) or 2 + eor 2 = 14 when V is set, then bpl. New = lda zp 3 + cmp# 2 + lda zp 3 + eor# 2 + sbc# 2 = 12, then bcc. That is 1 cycle saved in the V-clear case and 2 in the V-set case; if var were absolute instead of zero page the figures are 15 vs 14, so the saving holds either way. Bytes: 14 -> 12. Correctness: cmp/eor leave C untouched between the low-byte cmp and the high-byte sbc, so this is the standard biased unsigned compare; checked against var = -8, -7, 4, -1000, $7FFF and $8000 with imm = -8 and it gives the right answer at every boundary including the signed extremes, which is the case the old bvc/eor form exists to handle. Anonymous labels: the old body defines one `:` (the `bvc :+` target); the new body defines one `:` placeholder, exactly as blt16i and bge16i do, so the count past this macro is unchanged -- this matters because logic.s:2458 passes `:+` as the label argument to the sibling macro bgt16i. Registers/flags after the macro: A and N/Z differ from before, and C is now meaningful, but all six call sites (logic.s 1656, 1690, 1692, 2229, 2294, 2582) and all five branch targets (@j20 `lda #20`, @nocatch `lda bcnt`, @coll `add16` which starts clc, @done `rts`, @nostomp `lda hurt`, plus the fall-throughs `bge16i`/`mov16`/`sub16i`/`lda vy+1`) begin with a load or a sec/clc, so nothing reads A or the flags. Path frequency: this is the whole macro body, so the saving applies on every one of the six expansions, each executed once per frame per live object of that type (boomerang catch test, snake, walker stomp test). The same imm+1 substitution would convert bgt16i to bge16i's form for its single call site, but its first four instructions lie above this window so it is not proposed here.

original:

        lda t16+1                   ; <LV_OBJS = 0: only the high byte moves
        clc
        adc #>LV_OBJS
        sta t16+1
proposal:
add16 t16, t16b
        clc                         ; <LV_OBJS = 0: only the high byte moves
        adc #>LV_OBJS
        sta t16+1
argument: add16 dst, src expands to clc / lda dst / adc src / sta dst / lda dst+1 / adc src+1 / sta dst+1, so it leaves A holding exactly the new t16+1 that was just stored. The very next instruction reloads that same byte. Deleting the 'lda t16+1' is safe: the following 'clc' overwrites C (which the add16 left in an unknown state, so the clc must stay), and 'adc #>LV_OBJS' overwrites N,V,Z, so no flag set by the deleted load is consumed. X and Y are untouched by both versions. 3 cycles (lda zp) and 2 bytes. Path: this is the straight-line head of level_init's per-object record decode -- it executes exactly once per object in the level, on every path through the loop, so it is the busiest line in this window (the 'lda #0' + ten 'sta O_*,y' block below it also runs once per object and has no shorter form: stz has no abs,y addressing mode on the 65C02, so the lda #0 / sta abs,y sequence is already minimal). The saving is small in absolute terms because level_init runs once per level load, not per frame.

assumption: X is the @d loop counter, 4 down to 0, so X+4 <= 8 and the three asls cannot carry out.
original:

        clc
        adc #4                      ; score digits are slots 4..8
        tay
        txa
        asl
        asl
        asl
        adc #108
        tax
proposal:
txa
        clc
        adc #4                      ; score digits are slots 4..8
        tay
        asl
        asl
        asl
        adc #76                     ; (X+4)*8 + 76 = X*8 + 108
        tax
argument: One path only -- the body of the @d loop, run once per score digit, five times per draw_score call. The routine computes two things from the loop counter X (4 down to 0): Y = X+4 and A = 8X+108, and reloads X with 'txa' to do it. But 8X+108 = 8(X+4)+76, so the second txa is redundant: shift the X+4 that is already in A after 'tay' and adjust the constant. Original: txa 2 + clc 2 + adc #4 2 + tay 2 + txa 2 + asl 2 + asl 2 + asl 2 + adc #108 2 + tax 2 = 20. Proposal drops the second txa: 18. Saving 2 cycles and 1 byte per digit, 10 cycles per draw_score call. Carry: X is 0..4 so X+4 is 4..8 and the three asls see 8, 16, 32 at most -- no carry out, so 'adc #76' adds C = 0 exactly as the original 'adc #108' relied on C = 0 after shifting 8X<=32. The result 108..140 is identical, and 8(X+4) <= 64 never carries, so nothing else changes. Y is set before the shifts and is untouched by them. The flags left by tax are the same value's N,Z in both versions and are dead anyway -- 'lda q1' follows immediately.

assumption: X is dead after @fr, and A and C are dead after sta q1. Checked in logic.s:2446-2452: the next instruction is bge16 px, ox, :+ (lda px / cmp ox / lda px+1 / sbc ox+1 / bvc / eor / bpl), which sets its own carry with cmp and never reads X; then inc q1 / mov16 spy, oy / add16 spy, rise / lda q1 / jsr m_addsprite, none of which reads X either.

ldx #0
        lda fa
        bmi @fr
        ldx #2
        cmp #0                      ; A still holds fa; ldx did not touch it
        beq @fr
        ldx #4
@fr:    txa
        clc
        adc #54
        sta q1
proposal:
ldx #54
        lda fa
        bmi @fr
        ldx #56
        cmp #0                      ; A still holds fa; ldx did not touch it
        beq @fr
        ldx #58
@fr:    stx q1
argument: The three arms load X with 0, 2 or 4 and the join then does txa / clc / adc #54 / sta q1, i.e. the only use of X is as an index-into-a-constant that is immediately biased by 54. Biasing the three immediates at assembly time instead (54, 56, 58) makes the join a single stx q1. ldx #imm still does not disturb A, so the cmp #0 that re-derives Z from fa after ldx #56 is still needed and is left in place, and bmi/beq still read the flags of lda fa exactly as before. q1 is zero page ($C3, logic.s:267), so stx q1 is 2 bytes / 3 cycles against txa 2 + clc 2 + adc # 2 + sta q1 3 = 9 cycles / 6 bytes: 6 cycles and 4 bytes saved. The resulting q1 value is identical on all three arms (54/56/58, later incremented to 55/57/59 by the inc q1 below), matching the ldx #54 / ldx #55 / stx q1 idiom already used in the @knocked block twenty lines further down. Exit differences: A now holds fa rather than 54/56/58 and C is no longer forced to 0, both dead per the assumption above; X now holds the sprite id rather than 0/2/4, also dead. No branch target moves and no anonymous label is added or removed (@fr is a named cheap label and the ':' in the following bge16 is untouched). Path changed and frequency: the @draw arm with q6 non-zero, taken once per live red snake per frame -- but note the window's cost rank is 0, i.e. ob_rsnake does not run in the measured scene at all, so this is 6 cycles per execution on a path that may cost nothing today.

        lda oy

        sta spy+1

@basket:
        mov16 spx, ox
        mov16 spy, oy
        lda #60
        jmp m_addsprite
@knocked:
        bgt16i fc, -256, :+
        jmp @done

        bne :+
        add16i fd, 16

        bgt16 ox, px, :+

argument: Two surviving mov16+add16 pairs, one on each of ob_rsnake's two draw paths. 'mov16 spy, oy' is lda oy 3 + sta spy 3 + lda oy+1 3 + sta spy+1 3 = 12 cycles / 8 bytes, and 'add16 spy, rise' is clc 2 + lda spy 3 + adc rise 2 + sta spy 3 + lda spy+1 3 + adc rise+1 2 + sta spy+1 3 = 18 / 13 bytes, so 30 cycles and 21 bytes for what the fused form does in clc 2 + lda oy 3 + adc rise 2 + sta spy 3 + lda oy+1 3 + adc rise+1 2 + sta spy+1 3 = 18 cycles and 13 bytes. That is 12 cycles and 8 bytes each, and the same applies verbatim to 'mov16 spy, oy / add16 spy, fc' on the @knocked path -- 12 cycles and 8 bytes there too, hence 16 bytes over the window. saving_cycles is quoted as 12 because the two sites are on mutually exclusive paths: the first runs when the snake is out of its basket (q6 != 0), the second only while fb != 0 (knocked). The intermediate value of spy is not observed between the mov16 and the add16, the carry chain is identical (clc then two adcs), and A and the flags at the end are the same as before (the adc of the high byte, then sta). Anonymous labels: the ':' that 'bge16 px, ox, :+' targets is preserved on the new 'clc' line, and every other ':' line in the quoted run (the @knocked fd/ldx ladder) is reproduced unchanged, so the count and the targets of ':+' / ':++' are untouched. Note the ladder at 'ldx #54 / bgt16 / bra '+ / : ldx #55' could also be flattened to 'ldx #55 / bgt16 / ldx #54' for 1-2 cycles and 2 bytes, but that deletes an anonymous label, and this routine did not execute at all in the profile, so it is not worth the retargeting risk.

original:
:       ldx #54
        bgt16 ox, px, :+
        bra :++
:       ldx #55
:       stx q1
proposal:
:       ldx #54
        bge16 px, ox, :+
        ldx #55
:
:       stx q1
argument:
Path changed: the @knocked arm of ob_rsnake, which draws the knocked-back snake. It is cold (cost rank 0 - the profiler never saw it), so the honest value is the 2 bytes plus 1-2 cycles whenever a snake is knocked; I am flagging it because it is a free and provable rewrite, not because it is worth much.
`bgt16 ox, px, :+` expands to `lda px / cmp ox / lda px+1 / sbc ox+1 / bvc :+ / eor #$80 / : bmi :+`, computing px - ox and branching when ox > px (select sprite 55). `bge16 px, ox, :+` expands to `lda px / cmp ox / lda px+1 / sbc ox+1 / bvc :+ / eor #$80 / : bpl :+`, the SAME subtraction with the exact complementary condition px >= ox. So the taken/not-taken arms swap, the `ldx #55` moves onto the fall-through, and the `bra :++` that only existed to jump over it disappears.
Anonymous labels: this is the part to check. The original has, between the macro and `stx q1`, two `:` lines (`: ldx #55` and `: stx q1`); the proposal also has two (a bare `:` and `: stx q1`), and each macro body contributes exactly one `:` either way. The count is therefore unchanged and no `:+`/`:-` above or below is retargeted. Within the macro, `bvc :+` still lands on the macro's own `:`, and the passed `:+` still counts forward from the final branch to the first `:` after the macro - which in the proposal is the bare `:` placed after `ldx #55`, exactly where control must land when sprite 54 is kept. The bare `:` is deliberately kept rather than deleted, in the same style as the 'KEPT, unreferenced' label in drawrect.
Cycles: px >= ox arm, old = bmi not taken (2) + bra (3) = 5, new = bpl taken (3) = 3, saving 2; ox > px arm, old = bmi taken (3) + ldx (2), new = bpl not taken (2) + ldx (2), saving 1. Bytes: the 2-byte `bra` is removed.
Registers/flags: X is set on both arms exactly as before and is consumed by the following `stx q1`; A and the flags are dead (the next instruction after `stx q1` is `mov16 spy, oy`, which starts with an `lda`).
Verified: a patched copy of the tree assembles cleanly under ca65 --cpu 65C02 and links, with the segment shrinking by exactly the predicted byte count.

original:
mov16i spy, 4
        lda #TP_YOU
        jsr draw_piece
        mov16i spx, 82
        mov16i spy, 4
        lda #TP_WIN
        jsr draw_piece
proposal:
lda #4
        sta spy
        stz spy+1
        lda #TP_YOU
        jsr draw_piece
        lda #82
        sta spx
        stz spx+1
        lda #4
        sta spy
        stz spy+1
        lda #TP_WIN
        jsr draw_piece
argument:
Path changed: the win arm of winlose, executed once per completed game. The cycle figure is therefore of no practical value; the 6 bytes are the point.
All three `mov16i` immediates here (4, 82, 4) have a zero high byte, so each expands to `lda #imm` (2) / `sta X` (3) / `lda #0` (2) / `sta X+1` (3) = 10 cycles, 8 bytes, where `lda #0 / sta X+1` (2+3 cycles, 2+2 bytes) is exactly `stz X+1` (3 cycles, 2 bytes) on the 65C02 - spx is zero page at $33 and spy at $35. Each rewrite saves 2 cycles and 2 bytes; three of them gives 6 cycles and 6 bytes. Verified by assembling a patched copy of the tree with ca65/ld65: clean assembly, LOGIC segment shrinks by exactly the predicted amount. This is literally the encoding the @lose arm immediately below already uses (`lda #34 / sta spx / stz spx+1`), so the idiom is established in this routine.
Correctness: `stz` never touches A on a 65C02, and the value left in A differs from the original (4 or 82 instead of 0) - but in every case the very next instruction is `lda #TP_YOU` / `lda #4` / `lda #82` / `lda #TP_WIN`, so neither A nor the flags are live across any of the three sites. The final `lda #TP_WIN / jsr draw_piece` is quoted unchanged to anchor the run (there are three `mov16i spy, 4` in menu.s; this seven-line run is unique). No branches, no anonymous labels, and the spx/spy write order is preserved, so draw_piece sees identical arguments.

original:
blt16 fc, fa, :+
        bra @ydir
:       inc fc
        bne @ydir
        inc fc+1
        bra @ydir
@rxpos: beq16 rx, @ydir
        beq16 fc, @ydir
        bmi16 fc, @ydir
        lda fc
        bne :+
        dec fc+1
:       dec fc
@ydir:  bpl16 ry, @rypos
        blt16 fd, fb, :+
        bra @boom
proposal:
bge16 fc, fa, @ydir
:       inc fc
        bne @ydir
        inc fc+1
        bra @ydir
@rxpos: beq16 rx, @ydir
        beq16 fc, @ydir
        bmi16 fc, @ydir
        lda fc
        bne :+
        dec fc+1
:       dec fc
@ydir:  bpl16 ry, @rypos
        bge16 fd, fb, @boom
argument: Path changed: both chase arms, each executed once per live bat per step -- the two are reached on complementary halves of `bpl16 rx` / `bpl16 ry`, so between them one of the two edits is on every pass through ob_bat. blt16 and bge16 have identical expansions (lda/cmp/lda/sbc/bvc :+/eor #$80/: bXX label) except for the final bmi against bpl, so `blt16 fc, fa, :+ / bra @ydir` -- branch to the next instruction-pair if fc < fa, else jump to @ydir -- is exactly `bge16 fc, fa, @ydir` with the bra deleted. Cycles: when fc >= fa the old form paid bmi-not-taken 2 + bra 3 = 5 and the new pays bpl-taken 3, saving 2; when fc < fa the old paid bmi-taken 3 and the new pays bpl-not-taken 2, saving 1. Same for fd/fb. 2 bytes saved at each site. Anonymous labels: each macro expansion still contains exactly one `:` (its own bvc target), and the `:` lines on `inc fc` and `inc fd` are kept even though nothing now references them, so the count every other `:+`/`:-` in the routine walks past is unchanged. The label argument that was passed in (`:+`) is replaced by a named label, which cannot be miscounted. Registers and flags are unaffected: the macros clobber A and the flags either way, and the fall-through target is `inc fc` / `inc fd`, which read neither.

original:
lda #$FF
        sta lastkeys
        stz tmp3                    ; animation counter
        lda #$FF
        sta tmp2                    ; last drawn frame
proposal:
lda #$FF
        sta lastkeys
        sta tmp2                    ; last drawn frame
        stz tmp3                    ; animation counter
argument:
Two variables are seeded with the same $FF and a third with 0, but the stz is sequenced between them so the $FF has to be loaded twice. stz on a 65C02 does not touch A (macros.txt records this for stza), so sinking the stz below the second store lets the one `lda #$FF` serve both, dropping the second load: 2 cycles and 2 bytes.

Correctness: lastkeys, tmp2 and tmp3 are three distinct locations with no aliasing and no ordering requirement between them -- all three are being initialised before the @loop that follows. Flags: the original leaves N=1, Z=0 from the second `lda #$FF` (stz sets nothing, sta sets nothing); the proposal leaves N=1, Z=0 from the first `lda #$FF` for exactly the same reason. Identical. In any case the next instruction is `@loop: lda tmp4`, which reloads flags, and @loop is only ever entered with a fresh load at its head. No anonymous labels are involved.

Which path, how often: this is the one-shot setup before winlose's @loop, executed once per win/lose screen. The cycle saving is therefore negligible in frame terms -- I am proposing it for the 2 bytes and because it is free and unconditionally correct, not because it is hot. The window's cost rank is 0. I also considered `lda #84 / ldx #84` -> `ldx #84 / txa` at the two draw_number call sites (1 byte each, 0 cycles) and rejected it as not worth the churn.

assumption: @past is referenced only by the jmp being removed, and @one only by the bcs/beq a few lines above -- both verified over the whole of build_sections.
original:
sec
        sbc tmp2
        sta tmp4
        sta tmp2
        jsr @emit
        jmp @past
@one:   lda tmp4
        sta tmp2
        jsr @emit
@past:  lda tmp4
proposal:
sec
        sbc tmp2
        sta tmp4
@one:   lda tmp4
        sta tmp2
        jsr @emit
@past:  lda tmp4
argument: The split-run tail and @one end in the same three instructions: set tmp2 from the remaining row count, call @emit, continue at @past. After 'sta tmp4' the split path has exactly the state @one expects (tmp4 = rows still to emit), so it can fall straight into @one instead of duplicating 'sta tmp2 / jsr @emit' and then jumping over @one to @past. Correctness: @one's 'lda tmp4' reloads the value 'sta tmp4' just wrote, so tmp2 gets the same byte the deleted 'sta tmp2' would have stored; A is reloaded rather than carried, and no flags are consumed (the next instruction is sta). @past keeps its position immediately after @one's jsr, so 'lda tmp4' there still sees the full run length on the @one path and the remainder on the split path, exactly as before; the label becomes unreferenced but harmless. Cycles are a wash -- the jmp @past (3) is traded for @one's lda tmp4 (3) -- but 8 bytes go: sta tmp2 (2), jsr @emit (3), jmp @past (3). Path: the split arm of @run, taken once per frame whenever the 31-row playfield run crosses the ring end. Reported as a byte-only win, not a cycle win.

assumption: Only the three arms shown reach @fr (verified across all of ob_bat), so folding the +61 into their immediates covers every entry.
argument: @fr is reached from exactly three places, each of which has just loaded a constant (4, 0 or 2), so the constant add that follows can be done at assembly time: 4+61 = 65, 0+61 = 61, 2+61 = 63. The clc was there only to make adc safe with an unknown carry; with the add gone it goes too. The label @fr has to move onto 'sta q1', which is why that line is included in the edit. Correctness: q1 receives the same byte on all three arms; no flags are consumed, since the next instruction is bgt16 spx, px, :+ which begins 'lda px' and rebuilds N/V/Z from scratch, and sta sets no flags at all; the anonymous labels used just below (:+ / :++ in the bgt16 sequence) are untouched. Saves clc (2) + adc #imm (2) = 4 cycles and 3 bytes. Path: the @draw tail, which every call to ob_bat reaches -- all four early-out branches in the collision code jump to @draw -- so it is once per live bat per frame.

assumption: @f0, @f2 and @fr are cheap local labels reached only from the three branches shown in this block (verified against logic.s: the only references are the 'bcc @f0', 'bcc @f2' and the two 'bra @fr' immediately above).
argument: Every path into @fr arrives with A equal to one of three assembly-time constants (4, 0 or 2), and @fr's only job is to add the constant 61. Folding the addition into the three 'lda #' immediates deletes 'clc' (2 cycles, 1 byte) and 'adc #61' (2 cycles, 2 bytes) outright - 4 cycles and 3 bytes on every execution of the @draw path, which is the single path through this part of ob_bat and runs once per live bat per frame. Correctness: the immediates 0/2/4 + 61 = 61/63/65 all fit in a byte with no carry, and the original 'clc' guaranteed no incoming carry was added, so the results are identical. Flags: 'adc #61' set N/Z from the sum; after the rewrite the flags are those of the 'lda #', i.e. N/Z from the same value in the 4- and 2- arms and differing only in the 0/61 arm where Z went from set to clear. Those flags are dead: the very next instruction is 'sta q1' (no flag effect) and then 'bgt16 spx, px, :+' whose first instruction is 'lda px'. The anonymous-label count is unchanged - no ':' line is added or removed. Note the following 'bgt16 spx, px, :+ / bra :++' could also drop its 'bra' by inverting to 'bge16 px, spx, :+', worth a further 1-2 cycles and 2 bytes, but that changes how many anonymous labels the region contains and I am not proposing it.

assumption: glyph_index's only caller (menu.s:33, jsr glyph_index / jsr draw_glyph) uses the returned A only; draw_glyph opens with stza w16b+1 / asl and never reads the incoming carry. Verified by grep: line 33 is the sole call site.
original:
cmp #'A'
        bcc @notalpha
        cmp #'Z'+1
        bcs @notalpha
        sec
        sbc #'A'
        rts
@notalpha:
        cmp #'>'
        bne :+
        lda #26
        rts
:       cmp #'<'
        bne :+
        lda #27
        rts
:       cmp #'/'
        bne :+
        lda #28
        rts
:       cmp #'.'
        bne :+
        lda #29
        rts
:       sec
        sbc #'0'
        clc
        adc #30
        rts
proposal:
cmp #'A'
        bcc @notalpha
        cmp #'Z'+1
        bcs @notalpha
        sbc #('A'-1)                ; bcs not taken, so C = 0: subtracts 'A'-1+1 = 'A'
        rts
@notalpha:
        cmp #'>'
        bne :+
        lda #26
        rts
:       cmp #'<'
        bne :+
        lda #27
        rts
:       cmp #'/'
        bne :+
        lda #28
        rts
:       cmp #'.'
        bne :+
        lda #29
        rts
:       sec
        sbc #('0'-30)               ; -'0'+30 folded into one subtraction
        rts
argument: Two folds, no change to the anonymous-label count (four ':' lines before and after). (1) Alpha path: the sec is dead. It is reached only by falling through cmp #'Z'+1 / bcs @notalpha, so C is already 0 there; with C=0, sbc #('A'-1) computes A-('A'-1)-1 = A-'A', the same result, the same N/Z, and the same carry-out (1, since the result is non-negative for 'A'<=A<='Z'). Saves 2 cycles and 1 byte. (2) Digit path: sec / sbc #'0' / clc / adc #30 computes A-48+30 = A-18; sec / sbc #('0'-30) is sec / sbc #18, the same A-18, same N/Z from the same result. The carry-out differs (borrow out of A-18 rather than carry out of (A-48)+30) but nothing consumes it: the caller's next act is jsr draw_glyph, which starts stza w16b+1 / asl and generates its own carry. Saves 4 cycles and 2 bytes. Paths: (1) is the letters arm, which is what nearly all menu text is, so 2 cycles per character drawn; (2) is the digits arm, 4 cycles per digit. Both are cold -- glyph_index runs only from drawtext during menu/HUD text repaints -- so the absolute value is small, but both rewrites are free and provably flag-safe.

assumption: frame, t16 and obj are all zero page (frame at the logic.s .zeropage block, t16 = $D1, obj = $C9), and no branch targets a label inside this run (there is none between `lda frame` and `lsr t16`).
original:
lda frame
        asl
        sta t16
        lda frame+1
        rol
        sta t16+1                   ; t16 = 2*frame
        asl16 t16                   ; t16 = 4*frame
        add16 t16, frame            ; 5*frame
        lsr t16
        lsr t16
proposal:
lda frame
        asl
        asl                         ; A = 5*frame, low byte only: the high byte of
        clc                         ; 5*frame is dead (the >>2 below shifts the low
        adc frame                   ; byte alone, and sx16 t16 rewrites both bytes)
        lsr
        lsr
        sta t16
argument: ORIGINAL IS EXTENDED TWO LINES ABOVE THE WINDOW START (logic.s 2629-2630, `lda frame` / `asl`) because the rewrite folds them into the new shift chain.  The whole 16-bit computation of 5*frame is wasted: after it, `lsr t16` / `lsr t16` shift only the LOW byte (zeros in, t16+1 untouched), the result is consumed by a single `adc t16` followed by `and #15`, and `sx16 t16` further down rewrites both t16 and t16+1 -- so t16+1 is never read between here and that rewrite, and only bits 0..3 of (low byte >> 2) survive, i.e. bits 2..5 of the low byte of 5*frame.  The low byte of 5*frame depends only on the low byte of frame, so the high half can be dropped outright.  Original cost: lda frame 3 + asl 2 + sta t16 3 + lda frame+1 3 + rol 2 + sta t16+1 3 + asl16 (asl zp 5 + rol zp 5) + add16 (clc 2 + lda zp 3 + adc zp 3 + sta zp 3 + lda zp 3 + adc zp 3 + sta zp 3) + lsr zp 5 + lsr zp 5 = 56 cycles, 31 bytes.  New: lda frame 3 + asl 2 + asl 2 + clc 2 + adc frame 3 + lsr 2 + lsr 2 + sta t16 3 = 19 cycles, 11 bytes -- 37 cycles and 20 bytes saved.  A = 4*frame_lo after the two asls; clc + adc frame gives 5*frame_lo mod 256 exactly as before; two accumulator lsrs shift in zeros exactly as the two `lsr t16` did.  Carry out of `adc frame` is consumed and cleared by the lsrs and in any case the following code does `sec` then `clc` before each use.  N/Z are dead (`lda obj` is next).  No anonymous label touched.  This is the unconditional bat-wobble path, executed once per bat per frame.

assumption: The caller does not read flags on return -- verified: drawtext does `jsr glyph_index / jsr draw_glyph`, and draw_glyph opens with `stza w16b+1` (stz sets no flags) then `asl`, which sets its own.

The anonymous label on the `sec` line is preserved verbatim, so the ca65 `:+` counting in glyph_index's chain of four `bne :+` tests is unchanged.  This is the digit arm of glyph_index, the fall-through reached for any character that is not A-Z, '>', '<', '/' or '.', i.e. every digit drawn by draw_number -- the most-taken arm of the routine, though the routine itself is menu/HUD text and cold relative to the renderer.

        cmp #8

        sbc fa
        lsr

        adc #85

@done:  rts
proposal:
@draw:  lda fa
        bmi @done
        cmp #8
        bcc :+
        lda #23
        sec
        sbc fa
        lsr
        clc                         ; only the lsr can leave C set; bcc arrives with C=0

        jmp m_addsprite
@done:  rts
argument: Path changed: the fa < 8 arm of ob_spike's draw tail -- the spike's rising/falling animation frames, taken every frame the spike is in its 8-step active window (the fa >= 8 arm is the long dormant hold). 'bcc :+' is taken exactly when cmp #8 left C = 0, so that arm reaches the join with C already clear and the 'clc' is dead work. Only the other arm needs it, because 'lsr' shifts bit 0 of (23 - fa) into C. Moving the clc above the anonymous label -- so it sits after the lsr and the ':' now labels 'adc #85' -- makes the fa < 8 path 2 cycles shorter and leaves the fa >= 8 path identical (lsr/clc/adc, same order, same count). Byte count is unchanged: the clc is moved, not added. The anonymous-label count is unchanged -- there is still exactly one ':' between 'bcc :+' and 'adc #85', so :+ still resolves to the same construct, now one instruction later, which is precisely the intent. Flags: adc's result feeds m_addsprite as a sprite number in A, and the N/Z that adc sets are identical on both arms as before.

Byte-only win, no cycle change on either path. The two arms both end in `sta tmp3`, so sinking the store to the join point folds two `sta tmp3` (2 bytes each) into one and turns the 'always' `bne @pos` into `bra @pos`. Cycles: the #1 arm was lda 2 + sta 3 + bne-taken 3 = 8 and becomes lda 2 + bra 3 + sta 3 = 8; the @same arm was lda 2 + sta 3 = 5 and becomes lda 2 + fallthrough + sta 3 = 5. Both arms unchanged, so saving_cycles is honestly 0. Correctness: `sta` sets no flags and the next instruction is `ldy #1`, which sets its own, so nothing downstream reads flags across the join; `bra` is strictly safer than the `bne` that was relying on A=1 being non-zero; no anonymous label is added or removed. The compare chain below it (ldy/lda abs,x/cmp (rp),y, 2+4+5) has no cheaper form - swapping to `lda (rp),y / cmp SPRLIST+n,x` is the same 9 cycles and risks a page-cross penalty on the abs,x side.

assumption: Nothing references the anonymous label as `:-` from below (checked: there is no `:-` in logic.s between lines 1732 and 3070); the label count is unchanged either way.

        bcc :+

cmp #8
        bcc :+

Moving the `clc` above the label puts it on the arm that needs it and off the arm that does not: 2 cycles saved when fa < 8, 0 cost when fa >= 8, and the byte count is identical (the `:` and the `clc` simply swap lines). assumption: len*8 <= WINPX, i.e. the string is at most 20 characters - which is text_centred's own contract (x = (160 - len*8)/2 must be non-negative). The longest literal passed to it in menu.s is 19 characters (cursor_str/blank_str), so this holds today.
original:

        asl
        asl                         ; len*8
        eor #$FF                    ; WINPX - A, without parking A in memory
        sec
        adc #WINPX
        lsr
        jmp drawtext

asl
        asl                         ; len*4

argument: Path changed: the only path - every call to text_centred, once per centred string drawn (menus and the title screen, so cold; this is a 2-byte and 4-cycle win, not a hot-loop one). The routine computes (WINPX - 8*len)/2 with WINPX = ROWCHARS*2 = 160. Halving before the subtract instead of after gives the same answer: 80 - 4*len == (160 - 8*len)/2 exactly, because 160 - 8*len is always even. That drops the third `asl` (2 cy, 1 byte) and the trailing `lsr` (2 cy, 1 byte). WINPX/2 = 80 is exact at assembly time, and #(WINPX/2) is the byte value 80 - this is an 8-bit immediate throughout, so there is no #< / #> hazard. The complement-and-add idiom is unchanged in form: ~(4L) + 80 + 1 = 80 - 4L mod 256. The two forms diverge only when 8*len > 160, where the old code wraps modulo 256 after the subtract and the new one wraps modulo 512 before the halve - but that input is already a bug (the text does not fit the window) and both answers are garbage. Flags: drawtext's entry is `sta tx / stx ty / ldy #0` and reads neither carry nor N/Z, so the different carry out (adc leaves C=1 here, lsr left C=0) is not observed. The preceding `:` label on `tya` is untouched, so the anonymous-label count is unchanged.

assumption: vy is zero page (logic.s:218, inside the `.zeropage` block that starts at logic.s:213), so `stz vy` is the 3-cycle/2-byte zp form.
original:
:       mov16i vy, -1280
        lda #SFX_HIT
        sta SFXREQ
        rts

        lda #>(-1280)
        sta vy+1
        lda #SFX_HIT
        sta SFXREQ

The high byte is unchanged and still written through A, so the `#>` is kept as `#>(-1280)` and still assembles to $FB (the sibling bug of writing `#<` for the non-zero half is avoided - here it is genuinely the low half that is zero). Flags: mov16i leaves A = $FB with N set from `lda #>(-1280)`; the proposal leaves exactly the same, since `stz` sets no flags and the same `lda` follows. The next instruction is `lda #SFX_HIT` in both cases, so A is dead regardless. Path: the unconditional tail of player_hit, so every hit takes it - but player_hit runs only when an enemy connects, a handful of times per level, and the window's cost rank is 0. 2 cycles is honest and small.

assumption: drawrect reads only rc_x/rc_x+1/rc_y/rc_w/rc_h from this routine (it is entered the same way from @docols, @dorows and @full today), and the backward branch from @full to @dorows is ~17 bytes, comfortably inside bra range.

        sta rc_x+1

original:
mov16 t16, bvy
        asl16 t16
        add16 t16, bvy
proposal:
lda bvy
        asl
        sta t16
        lda bvy+1
        rol
        sta t16+1
        add16 t16, bvy
argument:
The butterfly integrator computes t16 = 3*v for both axes, but writes the two axes differently. For bvx (logic.s:1706-1711 in this same window) it uses the in-register form `lda bvx / asl / sta t16 / lda bvx+1 / rol / sta t16+1`; for bvy it uses `mov16 t16, bvy / asl16 t16`. The macro form copies the word to memory and then read-modify-writes it twice: mov16 is lda zp 3 + sta zp 3 + lda zp 3 + sta zp 3 = 12, asl16 is asl zp 5 + rol zp 5 = 10, total 22 cycles / 12 bytes. Doing the shift in the accumulator on the way through is 3 + 2 + 3 + 3 + 2 + 3 = 16 cycles / 10 bytes. -6 cycles, -2 bytes, and it makes the bvy path textually identical to the bvx path 17 lines above.

Equivalence: `asl` on A leaves C = bit 7 of bvy, exactly what `asl t16` would have left for `rol t16+1`, and `rol` on A then folds it into the high byte -- the same 16-bit left shift, with t16 never observed in its unshifted state (nothing reads it between the mov16 and the asl16 today). Registers: both forms clobber only A; X is live here (it is not -- `ldx #6` is set up after the following neg16 -- but neither form touches it either way) and Y is untouched by both. Flags on exit differ (old ended with `rol t16+1` setting N,Z and C from the high byte; new ends with `sta t16+1`, which sets none, with C left from the `rol` on A -- the same carry value), and this is safe because the very next line, `add16 t16, bvy`, begins with `clc` and then `lda`, so neither the flags nor C carry in. I include that add16 line unchanged in both strings so the match is anchored and unambiguous.

Frequency: this is the bfly physics arm of player_update, guarded by `lda bcnt / cmp #8 / bcc :+ / jmp @bfly` at the top of the window, so it runs at most once per frame and only while a butterfly is active -- the window's cost rank of 0 says it did not execute in the profiled run at all. 6 cycles per execution of the butterfly-physics path; the saving is small and I am reporting it because it is free and mirrors code already present, not because it is significant.

assumption: t16 and t16+1 are in zero page (as the asr16/neg16/add16 macro costs elsewhere in this routine assume), and nothing between the neg16 and the add16 reads t16+1 -- verified, the loop body is the only code there.
original:
neg16 t16
        ldx #6
:       asr16 t16
        dex
        bne :-
        add16 bvx, t16
proposal:
neg16 t16                   ; leaves A = t16+1
        ldx #6
:       cmp #$80
        ror
        ror t16
        dex
        bne :-
        sta t16+1
        add16 bvx, t16
argument: This is the bvx half of the boomerang physics. The bvy half, 15 lines below in the same routine, computes exactly the same thing and already uses the register-resident shift: `neg16 t16 / ldx #6 / : cmp #$80 / ror / ror t16 / dex / bne :- / sta t16+1`. The bvx half was left on the memory-resident `asr16 t16` macro. The conversion is mechanical and the bvy code is the proof it is correct. Why it works: neg16's last instruction is `sta var+1`, so A already holds t16+1 on exit (the bvy copy's comment says exactly this), and `ldx #6` does not disturb A. asr16 expands to `lda t16+1 / cmp #$80 / ror t16+1 / ror t16`: the cmp sets C from the sign bit, the first ror feeds that back into bit 7 (sign extension) and captures bit 0 into C, the second ror shifts it into t16's bit 7. Holding t16+1 in A gives the identical flag and data sequence -- `cmp #$80` on A, `ror` on A, `ror t16` -- and A is written back once after the loop. Cycle count, zero-page t16: old body = lda t16+1 3 + cmp# 2 + ror t16+1 5 + ror t16 5 + dex 2 + bne 3 = 20 per iteration, six iterations with the last branch not taken = 119. New body = cmp# 2 + ror A 2 + ror t16 5 + dex 2 + bne 3 = 14, six iterations = 83, plus one `sta t16+1` 3 = 86. Saving 33 cycles. Bytes: 13 -> 12. Path: this is straight-line code inside player_update's boomerang block, guarded only by `lda bcnt / cmp #8 / bcc :+ / jmp @bfly` a few lines above, so it executes once per frame whenever the boomerang is in flight, and there is no branch inside the window -- the 33 cycles are the whole window's saving, not an arm's. Flags after: the loop falls out of `bne :-` and the new `sta` sets none; the following `add16 bvx, t16` begins with clc, so nothing is consumed. Anonymous labels: one `:` before and one `:` after, so the `:-`/`:+` counting through this point is unchanged.

assumption: Nothing between this and the following 'sx16 t16' reads the low byte of bvy+128 -- which is what the existing comment on the first line asserts ('only the high byte of bvy+128 is ever used'), and the A produced by 'lda bvy / clc / adc #128' is in fact discarded by the very next instruction, 'lda bvy+1'.

        clc
        adc #128
        lda bvy+1
        adc #0
proposal:

        cmp #128
        lda bvy+1
        adc #0
argument: Path changed: straight-line code in the butterfly update, executed once per player_update while bactive is set (the window's cost rank is 0, so on the benchmark scene this never runs at all -- the saving is real but only pays when a butterfly is alive). The sequence computes bvy+128 as a 16-bit add and throws the low byte away, keeping only the carry into the high byte. 'clc / adc #128' produces C = 1 exactly when bvy >= 128, because 128 is the only bit that can carry out. 'cmp #128' sets C by the identical rule (C = 1 iff A >= operand) in one instruction: 2 cycles and 2 bytes instead of 4 cycles and 3 bytes. The A value differs (bvy vs bvy+128) but is destroyed unread by the 'lda bvy+1' on the next line, and N/Z are likewise overwritten by that load, so the only live output -- C feeding 'adc #0' -- is unchanged. Decimal mode is not a factor since cmp is unaffected by D and adc #0 still follows. 2 cycles, 1 byte.

assumption: inrange's only relevant output here is C, and @yes has exactly the two entries shown (fall-through from the second 'bcs @no', and the 'beq @yes' after 'lda bactive' which sits on the first 'bcs @no' fall-through).

        jsr inrange                 ; the boomerang overlaps it
        bcs @no
@yes:   lda q1
        clc
        adc #BOXN
        sta q1

        bcs @no
@yes:   lda q1                      ; both ways in fall through a 'bcs @no' that was not

        sta q1
